items.title: [Bug]: `TensorizerConfig(lora_dir=...)` leaves `tensorizer_dir=None` and breaks serialization round trips
items.body:
### Your current environment
The output of python collect_env.py ```text vLLM 0.30.0 and 0.28.0, CPU, Python 3.12, Ubuntu 24.04, x86_64 ```
### 🐛 Describe the bug `TensorizerConfig.__post_init__` derives `tensorizer_dir` only when `tensorizer_uri` is supplied explicitly. A configuration created using the documented LoRA-only form keeps `tensorizer_dir=None`. Code that writes the adapter then constructs a path such as `None/adapter_config.json`, and serializing and rebuilding the configuration changes its value. ```python from vllm.config.load import LoadConfig from vllm.model_executor.model_loader.tensorizer import TensorizerConfig from vllm.model_executor.model_loader.tensorizer_loader import TensorizerLoader tc = TensorizerConfig(lora_dir="/tmp/lora") print(tc.tensorizer_dir) # None print(f"{tc.tensorizer_dir}/adapter_config.json") # None/adapter_config.json loader = TensorizerLoader( LoadConfig( load_format="tensorizer", model_loader_extra_config={ "tensorizer_config": tc.to_serializable(), }, ) ) print(loader.tensorizer_config.tensorizer_dir) # /tmp/lora assert loader.tensorizer_config == tc # fails ``` ### Expected behavior A `lora_dir`-only configuration should resolve `tensorizer_dir` consistently, and `TensorizerConfig(**config.to_serializable())` should be equivalent to the original configuration. ### Suggested fix Derive `tensorizer_dir` from the resolved `tensorizer_uri` in all cases, including when that URI was inferred from `lora_dir`. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

items.title: [Bug]: xLAM tool parser (streaming) drops arguments nested deeper than two levels and truncates at a `}` inside a string
items.body:
### Your current environment
The output of python collect_env.py ```text vLLM 0.30.0 (the latest release) and 0.28.0, CPU, Python 3.12, Ubuntu 24.04, x86_64 ```
### 🐛 Describe the bug `xLAMToolParser.extract_tool_calls_streaming` extracts each call's `arguments` object with a regular expression that allows only one inner level of braces and ignores string literals. items.title: [Bug]: [KV Offload][P2P] A NIXL error raised by `write_blocks` during a fetch is never reported to the requesting peer, so it waits the full round timeout
items.body:
### Your current environment

- vLLM `0.30.0+g87ecf7d`, plus open PRs #56836 and #57139 and some local P2P hardening patches (see the note below).
- torch 2.13.0+cu130, CUDA 13.0, `nixl-cu13` 1.3.2 (UCX backend).
- 8× H100 80GB HBM3 per node, driver 580.126.20, RoCE.
- Model: GLM-5.3, disaggregated prefill/decode. Prefill is DP4 × PCP8, one DP rank per node, with `TieringOffloadingSpec`: a 512 GiB CPU primary tier plus a `p2p` secondary tier over UCX.

The code path below is unchanged on `main` (checked against `e11962fc1c`): our build's `session/server.py` is byte-identical to `main`, and `data/nixl.py`'s `write_blocks` is identical too.


### 🐛 Describe the bug


When the source side of a P2P fetch calls `NixlTransport.write_blocks` and NIXL raises (we saw `nixlRemoteDisconnectError` and `nixlNotFoundError`), the exception escapes to the session's message dispatcher, which only logs it. The requesting peer is never told the fetch failed. It waits for its round timeout (30 s here), aborts, and only then falls back to recomputing the prefix.

Call chain, from our traceback (line numbers from our build, same code on `main`):

```
session.py   _on_message            -> _dispatch_message
server.py    on_fetch               (line 390) -> self._submit_transfer(...)
server.py    _submit_transfer       (line 1072) -> self._transport.write_blocks(...)
nixl.py      write_blocks           (line 294) -> self._agent.transfer(handle)
nixl_cu13/_api.py transfer          (line 632) raises nixlRemoteDisconnectError / nixlNotFoundError
```

`_submit_transfer` already has a fail-fast path, but only for `write_blocks` *returning* `None` (no remote descriptor list for the peer). That path marks the round finishing and calls `_finalize_outbound(kv_request_id, round_key, success=False)` so that "the peer and the local store jobs don't wait for finish_request or for `_STORE_TIMEOUT_S` / `_LOAD_TIMEOUT_S`". A raised exception skips it. The dispatcher in `session.py` (`main` lines ~319-333) logs `error handling message 'fetch'`, increments `_dispatch_error_count` and continues. Nothing finalizes the round.

Observed on the source and requesting ranks for one pull (`kv_request_id` shortened):

```
05:16:26 source     P2PSession <requester>:7777: error handling message 'fetch' (count=1): NIXL_ERR_REMOTE_DISCONNECT
                      File ".../p2p/session/server.py", line 390, in on_fetch
05:16:56 requester  P2PSession <source>:7777: paircheck-5d88… round=0 timed out, sending abort
05:16:56 source     P2PSession <requester>:7777: store job 6883 timed out
05:16:57 requester  load request paircheck-5d88… (job_id=6864) completed with failure after abort
```

Impact: each affected request took 37 s, against about 6 s to recompute the ~113K-token prefix locally and about 3.4 s for a successful pull. With any persistent transfer failure (see issue 2), every pull touching the bad peer pays the full timeout, and there is no request error to surface it.

It also looks like the handle from `make_prepped_xfer` is not released when `transfer` raises, though we did not confirm this.

### Expected behavior

A NIXL error while submitting a fetch's write should be handled like the existing `write_blocks -> None` case: finalize the round with `success=False`, so the requester falls back to recompute immediately rather than after its timeout.

### Suggested fix

One of:

- catch NIXL errors in `NixlTransport.write_blocks` around `make_prepped_xfer` / `transfer`, release the handle, log, and return `None`, which reuses the existing fail-fast path; or
- in `P2PSession._submit_transfer`, wrap the `write_blocks` call and send exceptions to the same branch as `transfer_id is None`.

A unit test could make the transport's `write_blocks` raise and assert that the round is finalized with `success=False` and the peer is notified, without waiting for `_LOAD_TIMEOUT_S`.

### Reproduction

Any condition that makes `agent.transfer` raise on the source while the control session stays up reproduces it. We hit it after issue 2: a peer whose NIXL path had gone stale. In that state, every directed pull to or from the peer showed the trace above, which we confirmed with requests carrying `kv_transfer_params.remote_kv_source = {kv_request_id, remote_host, remote_port}`.

Related: #56836 (bounds unanswered *lookup* waits; does not cover this *fetch* failure), #57139.

items.title: [Bug]: `vllm preload` daemon never matches a dense (non-MoE) engine with `--data-parallel-size > 1` (WeightCacheKey `dp_size` mismatch)
items.body:
### Your current environment
The output of python collect_env.py ```text OS : Ubuntu 22.04.3 LTS (x86_64) Python : 3.12.14 PyTorch : 2.13.0+cu130 (CUDA 13.0) transformers : 5.17.0 GPUs : 2x NVIDIA RTX A6000 Nvidia driver : 580.178.04 vLLM : main at 5f30fc7031 (2026-10-03), built from source ```
### 🐛 Describe the bug With a dense (non-MoE) model and `--data-parallel-size N` (N > 1), engines started with `--load-format ipc_cache` never use the daemon started by `vllm preload` with the same flags. The daemon fingerprints each rank with `dp_size=N, dp_rank=r`, but a dense engine fingerprints every rank with `dp_size=1, dp_rank=0`, so the `WeightCacheKey` check fails on every rank. - With the default `fallback=true`, each rank logs one warning and loads from disk. The server works, but Fast Start does nothing, and the daemon keeps holding its own copy of the weights on every GPU. - With `"fallback": false`, the engine fails to start. The preload docs list data parallelism as supported ([`docs/features/preload.md` L26-L28](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/5f30fc7031cae49bf51073fc953d419b08f8887c/docs/features/preload.md#L26-L28), [L167](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/5f30fc7031cae49bf51073fc953d419b08f8887c/docs/features/preload.md#L167)) and do not restrict it to MoE models. #### Reproduction Two GPUs, public dense model. ```bash # Terminal 1 vllm preload --model Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --data-parallel-size 2 ``` Wait for `Weight cache daemon READY`, then: ```bash # Terminal 2 vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --data-parallel-size 2 --load-format ipc_cache \ --enforce-eager --gpu-memory-utilization 0.2 --max-model-len 2048 ``` `--enforce-eager`, `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.2` and `--max-model-len 2048` only keep the run small because the GPUs on my machine are shared. #### Results With the default `fallback=true`, the server starts and answers, but no rank logs `Mapped ... tensors from the weight cache daemon`. Instead: ```text (Worker pid=2698932) WARNING [ipc_loader.py:217] Weight cache unusable (WeightCacheKey mismatch on fields: ['dp_size']); falling back to disk loading (Worker pid=2698929) WARNING [ipc_loader.py:217] Weight cache unusable (WeightCacheKey mismatch on fields: ['dp_size', 'dp_rank']); falling back to disk loading ``` The daemon logs the same two mismatches and keeps serving. With `--model-loader-extra-config '{"fallback": false}'` added to `vllm serve`, `EngineCore failed to start`. Rank 0 raises `CacheConfigMismatchError: WeightCacheKey mismatch on fields: ['dp_size']`, rank 1 the same with `['dp_size', 'dp_rank']`.
Traceback with fallback=false (rank 0) ```text Traceback (most recent call last): File "vllm/v1/executor/multiproc_executor.py", line 915, in worker_main worker = WorkerProc(*args, **kwargs) ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ File "vllm/tracing/otel.py", line 175, in sync_wrapper return func(*args, **kwargs) ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ File "vllm/v1/executor/multiproc_executor.py", line 682, in __init__ self.worker.load_model() File "vllm/v1/worker/gpu_worker.py", line 574, in load_model self.model_runner.load_model(load_dummy_weights=load_dummy_weights) File "vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py", line 379, in load_model self.model = model_loader.load_model( ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ File "vllm/tracing/otel.py", line 175, in sync_wrapper return func(*args, **kwargs) ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ File "vllm/model_executor/model_loader/weight_cache/ipc_loader.py", line 211, in load_model state = self._fetch_entries(model_config) ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ File "vllm/model_executor/model_loader/weight_cache/ipc_loader.py", line 359, in _fetch_entries return self._request_state_with_startup_wait(cache_config) ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ File "vllm/model_executor/model_loader/weight_cache/ipc_loader.py", line 365, in _request_state_with_startup_wait return self._with_startup_wait(lambda: self._request_state(cache_config)) ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ File "vllm/model_executor/model_loader/weight_cache/ipc_loader.py", line 373, in _with_startup_wait return op() ^^^^ File "vllm/model_executor/model_loader/weight_cache/ipc_loader.py", line 365, in return self._with_startup_wait(lambda: self._request_state(cache_config)) ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ File "vllm/model_executor/model_loader/weight_cache/ipc_loader.py", line 397, in _request_state raise CacheConfigMismatchError( vllm.model_executor.model_loader.weight_cache.protocol.CacheConfigMismatchError: WeightCacheKey mismatch on fields: ['dp_size'] ```
Two controls on the same machine: - The same commands without `--data-parallel-size` on one GPU: the engine logs `Mapped 339 tensors from the weight cache daemon (zero_copy mode)`. - One `vllm preload` **without** `--data-parallel-size` per GPU (`CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0` and `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1`), then the same `vllm serve ... --data-parallel-size 2 --load-format ipc_cache` with `fallback=false`: both ranks map 339 tensors from the daemon on their GPU and the server answers normally. So the daemons' weights are usable; only the advertised key differs. (This also works as a workaround.) #### Cause 1. For a non-MoE model, the engine runs every DP rank as an independent DP=1 engine: `run_engine_core` calls `parallel_config.reconfigure_for_independent_dp_rank()` ([`core.py` L1388-L1397](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/5f30fc7031cae49bf51073fc953d419b08f8887c/vllm/v1/engine/core.py#L1388-L1397)), which sets `data_parallel_size = 1` and `data_parallel_rank = 0` ([`parallel.py` L1158-L1167](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/5f30fc7031cae49bf51073fc953d419b08f8887c/vllm/config/parallel.py#L1158-L1167)). The Ray actor path does the same ([`core.py` L2631](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/5f30fc7031cae49bf51073fc953d419b08f8887c/vllm/v1/engine/core.py#L2631)). 2. The IPC loader builds its `WeightCacheKey` from `get_dp_group()`, so a dense engine sends `dp_size=1, dp_rank=0` on every GPU ([`ipc_loader.py` L345-L357](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/5f30fc7031cae49bf51073fc953d419b08f8887c/vllm/model_executor/model_loader/weight_cache/ipc_loader.py#L345-L357)). 3. The daemon builds its key from the launcher's `data_parallel_size` and its own `dp_rank`, regardless of the model ([`daemon.py` L189](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/5f30fc7031cae49bf51073fc953d419b08f8887c/vllm/model_executor/model_loader/weight_cache/daemon.py#L189), [L226-L237](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/5f30fc7031cae49bf51073fc953d419b08f8887c/vllm/model_executor/model_loader/weight_cache/daemon.py#L226-L237)). For `--data-parallel-size 2`: | GPU | daemon key | engine key | mismatched fields | |---|---|---|---| | 0 | `dp_size=2, dp_rank=0` | `dp_size=1, dp_rank=0` | `dp_size` | | 1 | `dp_size=2, dp_rank=1` | `dp_size=1, dp_rank=0` | `dp_size`, `dp_rank` | MoE models are not affected: their engines keep the real DP placement (`DPEngineCoreProc`), which is what the daemon advertises. #### Scope - Reproduced on `main` at `5f30fc7031` (2026-10-03). All code links above point at that commit. - Only tested on one node with TP=1 and the multiprocessing backend. Not tested: TP > 1 with DP, multi-node DP, MoE with DP, the Ray DP path, and draft daemons (speculative decoding) with DP. - `tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_weight_cache.py` checks the daemon's rank placement and the key comparison, but nothing checks the key a dense DP engine actually sends. #### Related - #57386 added data parallelism to the daemon. Its description targets DP + EP decode fleets; the dense DP=1 rescoping in the engine is not accounted for. - #56949 (closed) is the same class of problem in the RL weight-transfer path: dense DP engines reset `data_parallel_rank` to 0. #56950 fixed that path by reading `data_parallel_index` instead. > AI disclosure: this issue was investigated and drafted with an AI assistant (Claude). A human reviewed the issue before filing. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

items.title: [Bug]: NIXL pull: one wedged connection repeatedly strands decode KV blocks (production log analysis)
items.body:
### Your current environment

- Production: disaggregated P/D on a build based on v0.30.0, `nixl==1.4.1`, `NixlConnector` in pull mode, `kv_load_failure_policy: fail`, default `engine_ttl=3600`, mlx5 `rc` transport.
- Decode is TP2. Prefill is TP8/DCP8, so each decode request posts 16 READs (2 decode workers x 8 prefill ranks). About 40 prefill engines.
- The connector's NIXL agent is created without `sync_mode` (see #59870).

### Describe the bug

One decode engine leaked KV blocks in a staircase until it sat at ~97% utilization and stopped admitting anything but small requests. The decode pod's log shows the cause is **a single wedged connection**: one decode TP worker has a connection to one rank of one prefill engine on which no READ ever completes. Every request prefilled on that engine and routed to this decode engine loses the same READ, waits until the client gives up, is aborted, and leaves its blocks pinned.

This is the production case behind #59872. That issue describes what vLLM does once a READ stays in `PROC`. This issue adds what the log shows about how it gets there and why it repeats.

#### What each episode looks like

Stats lines normally report successful transfers in multiples of 16. Each episode starts with one that is one short, followed by ~45 minutes with no engine activity, after which the KV floor has risen:

```
08:08:38 Engine 012: Running: 0 reqs, Waiting: 1 reqs, Deferred: 1 reqs, GPU KV cache usage: 5.5%
08:08:38 KV Transfer metrics: Num successful transfers=15, ..., Num failed transfers=0
08:53:38 Engine 012: Running: 0 reqs, Waiting: 0 reqs, GPU KV cache usage: 5.5%
```

| Stuck at (UTC) | Transfers in that line | Silence after | KV floor after |
|---|---|---|---|
| 08:08:38 | 15 | 45m00s | 5.5% |
| 09:16:38 | 15 | 45m10s | 8.6% |
| 12:24:18 | 15 | 45m21s | 30.9% |
| 13:14:39 | 15 | 45m30s | 36.3% |
| 14:22:29 | 31 | 45m10s | 38.9% |
| 15:38:39 | 31 | 44m50s | 63.1% |
| 16:28:59 | 15 | 45m10s | 65.2% |
| 17:19:39 | 31 | 45m00s | 67.0% |
| 18:16:39 | 15 | 45m00s | 76.3% |
| 19:28:29 | 31 | 21m20s | 95.3% |

`Num failed transfers` stays 0 and nothing is logged. The ~2,700 s wait matches an upstream timeout; the request is aborted at that point (inferred, the log has no abort line). While it waits, the engine receives no other traffic.

#### It is one connection, not random loss

- **Only one of four engines in the pod is affected.** Same build, same prefill peers, same transfer latency and throughput.

  | Engine | Successful READs | Stat silences > 10 min | KV floor at end |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | affected | 11,597 | 56 | 83% |
  | sibling 1 | 220,033 | 0 | 0% |
  | sibling 2 | 221,404 | 0 | 0% |
  | sibling 3 | 219,944 | 0 | 0% |

- **One prefill engine is never evicted by TP0.** For every other live prefill engine, the affected engine's two workers evict in lockstep (for example 15 and 14 times). For one engine, TP1 evicted it 9 times and TP0 never did in 58 hours. `_evict_stale_engines` skips engines in `_engines_with_inflight_transfers`, so TP0 has had a READ outstanding to that engine the whole time.
- **TP1 re-handshakes alone, then a request sticks.** There are 8 handshake bursts where only TP1 handshook (8 log lines, not 16). Two of them are 2 to 5 s before a stuck request.
- **If READs were lost at random, about ten different prefill engines would be held.** Exactly one is.
- **The rate fits one engine's share of traffic.** A mean of 61 requests completed between stuck events, with ~40 prefill engines.
- **It was broken from first use.** The first stuck request came 4 s after a handshake burst, 19 minutes after the pod started and before any eviction. That this handshake was with the held engine is inferred; the handshake log lines carry no engine id.

#### Why it never recovers

1. NIXL reports `PROC` for as long as UCX reports the request in progress. In NIXL 1.4.1 `nixlUcxEngine::checkXfer` relays `ucp_request_check_status` and has no deadline. UCX only fails a request when the transport reports the endpoint failed.
2. The pull path has no deadline either (#59872), so the request waits until the client aborts.
3. On abort the scheduler delays the free until every worker reports `finished_recving`, which never happens.
4. The stuck READ keeps the engine in `_engines_with_inflight_transfers`, so that worker never evicts and re-handshakes it. The broken connection is used again for the next request from the same prefill engine.

#### Knock-on effect

The leaking engine served 1,079 requests against ~14,100 on each sibling, so its prefill pairings went idle and were evicted far more often (285 evictions per worker against 57 to 74). Each eviction and re-handshake leaks UCX endpoints (#59956), and about 31 hours after the KV leak plateaued the same workers started failing handshakes.

### What is not established

- **Why the connection wedged.** Nothing is logged on the decode side. The timing (broken from the first READ after a handshake) points at connection setup, and the unsynchronized agent access in #59870 is the leading candidate, but it is not proven.
- **Which of the 8 prefill ranks it is.** The prefill pod's lease-expiry warnings (`Releasing expired KV blocks ... retrieved by N remote worker(s)`) should show it.

### Reproduction

**Wedged connection to leak (reproduces, CPU only).** A script drives the real `Scheduler` and the real NIXL pull worker with the repo's `FakeNixlWrapper`, modified so READs to one of two remote engines never leave `PROC`, and aborts each stuck request after a timeout. Requests from the healthy engine keep completing; usage only steps up.

| Req | Prefill engine | Blocks | Outcome | KV in use after |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1-2 | good | 60, 90 | completed | 0.0% |
| 3 | bad | 55 | aborted | 9.2% |
| 4 | good | 80 | completed | 9.2% |
| 5 | bad | 110 | aborted | 27.5% |
| 6-7 | good | 70, 50 | completed | 27.5% |
| 8 | bad | 85 | aborted | 41.7% |
| 9 | bad | 120 | aborted | 61.8% |
| 10 | good | 60 | completed | 61.8% |
| 11 | bad | 100 | aborted | 78.5% |
| 12 | good | 40 | completed | 78.5% |

470 blocks stay pinned, equal to the five requests from the bad engine, and the scheduler is left tracking five `FINISHED_ABORTED` requests.

**Handshake race to wedged connection (does not reproduce on TCP).** A standalone NIXL 1.4.1 harness (CPU memory, `UCX_TLS=tcp,self`, agent without `sync_mode`) runs a handshake thread loading new peers while a second thread polls notifications, sends heartbeats and posts READs, then tests the first READ on each new connection.

| Measure | Result |
|---|---|
| New connections tested | 48,520 |
| First READ completed | 48,512 |
| First READ raised on status check | 8 |
| First READ stuck in `PROC` | 0 |
| `NIXL_ERR_NOT_FOUND` from other calls during the race | 119 |

The race is visible as errors, but none produced a silently stuck handle. This was not run on `rc` with GPU memory.

Separately, a standalone test confirms NIXL has no transfer deadline: a READ posted to a peer that is connected but not progressing (`SIGSTOP`) stayed `PROC` for 90 s with no error and completed within about a second of `SIGCONT`. A killed peer raised `NIXL_ERR_REMOTE_DISCONNECT` immediately.

### Proposal

1. **Recover from a wedged connection, not only report it.** A pull-side deadline that fails the request (#59874 default) stops the 45-minute stalls but the next request from that prefill engine sticks again. After a deadline, the worker should drop and re-handshake that remote engine. This depends on NIXL closing the endpoint (#59956, ai-dynamo/nixl#2338) and on a guarantee that the stalled READ has stopped before its blocks are reused.
2. **Do not let a stuck READ pin an engine against eviction forever.** `_engines_with_inflight_transfers` currently guarantees a wedged connection is reused.
3. **Make it visible.** A gauge for KV pinned by transfers of finished requests (#58004), and an engine id on the handshake log lines.
4. **Close the agent race** (#59870, #59877) as the leading candidate for the trigger.

Operationally, restarting the decode pod is the only thing that clears it today.

### Related

- #59872 / #59874: aborted request whose READ never completes keeps its blocks; pull-side timeout.
- #59870 / #59877: one NIXL agent used from two threads without a sync mode.
- #59956: `remove_remote_agent` does not release UCX endpoints.
- #58004: gauges for KV cache pinned by pending KV transfers.

_AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to analyze the production log, write the reproducers and draft this issue. The numbers above are from that log and from runs of those reproducers._

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

items.title: [Bug]: NIXL: `remove_remote_agent` does not release UCX endpoints, so each `engine_ttl` eviction + re-handshake leaks until handshakes fail
items.body:
### Your current environment - vLLM `main` at `54020c3c3e`, `nixl==1.4.1` (`nixl-cu13` wheel, bundled UCX), Python 3.12. - Repro box: 8x H100, no RDMA NIC, so UCX uses `tcp` / `cuda_ipc` / `sm`. - Production deployment this came from: disaggregated P/D, `NixlConnector` (pull), decode TP2, each decode worker loads 8 remote agents per prefill engine, mlx5 `rc` transport, default `engine_ttl=3600`. ### Describe the bug `nixl_agent.remove_remote_agent()` (`invalidateRemoteMD`) returns success but does not destroy the UCX endpoints created by `add_remote_agent()` (`loadRemoteMD`). vLLM calls it for every agent in `_cleanup_remote_engine` (`nixl/base_worker.py:3525`) and assumes the transport resources come back. They do not, so every `engine_ttl` eviction followed by a re-handshake permanently leaks one UCX endpoint per UCX worker per remote rank in the decode worker process. **Production symptom.** After ~2,290 `add_remote_agent` calls (and ~280 evictions that had already removed ~2,250 of those agents), two decode workers hit a fixed ceiling two hours apart and every later handshake failed: ``` UCX madvise(DONTFORK, len=65536) failed: Resource temporarily unavailable (ib_mlx5.h, DEVX buffer alloc) -> UCX endpoint create failed -> loadRemoteMD NIXL_ERR_BACKEND -> handshake_setup_failed ``` That is consistent with per-QP DEVX buffers never being freed until the process reaches `vm.max_map_count`. Evictions after the wall freed nothing. The least-loaded decode rank failed first because idle pairings are the ones that get evicted and re-handshaken. **Standalone reproducer (no vLLM, no RDMA).** Two NIXL agents, UCX backend, `num_threads=4` as vLLM configures it. D loops `add_remote_agent -> prep_xfer_dlist -> READ -> release -> remove_remote_agent` and samples `/proc/self`: | mode | D-side growth per cycle | after 400 cycles | |---|---|---| | add + READ + remove | +5 fds, all TCP sockets in `ESTABLISHED` | 173 -> 2173 fds | | add + remove, no transfer | +4 fds | | | add + READ, never remove | 0 | | | 25 s idle after the loop, then one more READ | nothing is closed | | 5 = one endpoint per UCX worker (1 main + 4 progress threads); the main worker's endpoint is created lazily on first transfer. The P side stays flat. On mlx5 the same endpoints are QPs plus DEVX buffers, i.e. the VMA growth above. **Reproduced in vLLM.** DeepSeek-V2-Lite, P TP2/DCP2, D TP2 with `"kv_connector_extra_config": {"engine_ttl": 30}`. Each cycle = one P->D request, idle past the TTL, then a handshake to another engine so `_evict_stale_engines` runs. Sockets per decode worker: 85, 95, 105, 115, i.e. +10 per cycle (2 remote ranks x 5 endpoints), with "Evicted stale remote engine" logged each time. With 8 remote ranks that is 40 endpoints per re-handshake per worker.
nixl_add_remove_loop.py ```python """Standalone NIXL add_remote_agent / remove_remote_agent churn test. Mirrors what a vLLM decode worker does on every engine_ttl eviction + re-handshake: add_remote_agent -> prep_xfer_dlist(remote) -> READ -> release -> remove_remote_agent and samples per-process resources on the "D" side to see what remove does not return. .venv/bin/python nixl_add_remove_loop.py --iters 400 --every 50 [--no-xfer] """ import argparse import multiprocessing as mp import os import subprocess import time import torch BUF_BYTES = 256 << 20 BLOCK = 64 << 10 def sample(dgpu: int) -> dict: with open("/proc/self/maps") as f: maps = sum(1 for _ in f) with open("/proc/self/status") as f: st = dict(l.split(":", 1) for l in f.read().splitlines() if ":" in l) bar1 = subprocess.check_output( ["nvidia-smi", "-q", "-d", "MEMORY", f"--id={dgpu}"]).decode() bar1_used = [l for l in bar1.splitlines() if "Used" in l][1].split(":")[1].strip() kinds: dict[str, int] = {} for fd in os.listdir("/proc/self/fd"): try: tgt = os.readlink(f"/proc/self/fd/{fd}") except OSError: continue k = tgt.split(":")[0] if tgt.startswith(("socket", "anon_inode", "pipe")) else tgt.rsplit("/", 1)[0] kinds[k] = kinds.get(k, 0) + 1 inodes = set() for fd in os.listdir("/proc/self/fd"): try: t = os.readlink(f"/proc/self/fd/{fd}") except OSError: continue if t.startswith("socket:["): inodes.add(t[8:-1]) socks: dict[str, int] = {} for fam, path, icol, scol in (("tcp", "/proc/self/net/tcp", 9, 3), ("tcp6", "/proc/self/net/tcp6", 9, 3), ("unix", "/proc/self/net/unix", 6, None)): for line in open(path).read().splitlines()[1:]: cols = line.split() if cols[icol] in inodes: key = fam if scol is None else f"{fam}:{cols[scol]}" socks[key] = socks.get(key, 0) + 1 return dict(maps=maps, fds=sum(kinds.values()), fd_kinds=kinds, socks=socks, threads=int(st["Threads"]), rss=st["VmRSS"].strip(), bar1=bar1_used) def make_agent(name: str, num_threads: int): from nixl._api import nixl_agent, nixl_agent_config cfg = nixl_agent_config(num_threads=num_threads, capture_telemetry=True) return nixl_agent(name, cfg) def p_main(gpu: int, q_meta: mp.Queue, q_stop: mp.Queue): torch.cuda.set_device(gpu) agent = make_agent("P", 4) buf = torch.empty(BUF_BYTES, dtype=torch.uint8, device=f"cuda:{gpu}") descs = agent.get_reg_descs([(buf.data_ptr(), BUF_BYTES, gpu, "")], "VRAM") agent.register_memory(descs, backends=["UCX"]) q_meta.put((agent.get_agent_metadata(), buf.data_ptr(), gpu)) q_stop.get() print(f"P side at end: fds={len(os.listdir('/proc/self/fd'))} " f"sockets={sum(1 for fd in os.listdir('/proc/self/fd') if 'socket' in (os.readlink(f'/proc/self/fd/{fd}') if os.path.exists(f'/proc/self/fd/{fd}') else ''))}", flush=True) agent.deregister_memory(descs) def d_main(args, meta, raddr, rgpu): torch.cuda.set_device(args.dgpu) agent = make_agent("D", 4) buf = torch.empty(BUF_BYTES, dtype=torch.uint8, device=f"cuda:{args.dgpu}") reg = agent.get_reg_descs([(buf.data_ptr(), BUF_BYTES, args.dgpu, "")], "VRAM") agent.register_memory(reg, backends=["UCX"]) nblocks = BUF_BYTES // BLOCK local_h = agent.prep_xfer_dlist( "NIXL_INIT_AGENT", [(buf.data_ptr() + i * BLOCK, BLOCK, args.dgpu) for i in range(nblocks)], "VRAM") rdescs = [(raddr + i * BLOCK, BLOCK, rgpu) for i in range(nblocks)] ids = list(range(0, 64)) base = sample(args.dgpu) print(f"iter 0: {base}", flush=True) t0 = time.time() for it in range(1, args.iters + 1): name = agent.add_remote_agent(meta) rh = agent.prep_xfer_dlist(name, rdescs, "VRAM") if not args.no_xfer: xh = agent.make_prepped_xfer("READ", local_h, ids, rh, ids, b"n") agent.transfer(xh) while agent.check_xfer_state(xh) == "PROC": time.sleep(0.0005) agent.release_xfer_handle(xh) agent.release_dlist_handle(rh) if not args.no_remove: agent.remove_remote_agent(name) if it % args.every == 0: s = sample(args.dgpu) print(f"iter {it}: {s} (+{s['maps']-base['maps']} maps, " f"+{s['fds']-base['fds']} fds, {time.time()-t0:.1f}s)", flush=True) if args.settle: time.sleep(args.settle) s = sample(args.dgpu) print(f"after {args.settle}s idle: fds={s['fds']} sockets={s['fd_kinds'].get('socket')}", flush=True) name = agent.add_remote_agent(meta) rh = agent.prep_xfer_dlist(name, rdescs, "VRAM") xh = agent.make_prepped_xfer("READ", local_h, ids, rh, ids, b"n") agent.transfer(xh) while agent.check_xfer_state(xh) == "PROC": time.sleep(0.0005) agent.release_xfer_handle(xh) agent.release_dlist_handle(rh) agent.remove_remote_agent(name) time.sleep(2) s = sample(args.dgpu) print(f"after one more READ + 2s: fds={s['fds']} sockets={s['fd_kinds'].get('socket')}", flush=True) agent.release_dlist_handle(local_h) agent.deregister_memory(reg) if __name__ == "__main__": ap = argparse.ArgumentParser() ap.add_argument("--iters", type=int, default=400) ap.add_argument("--every", type=int, default=50) ap.add_argument("--pgpu", type=int, default=0) ap.add_argument("--dgpu", type=int, default=1) ap.add_argument("--no-xfer", action="store_true") ap.add_argument("--no-remove", action="store_true") ap.add_argument("--settle", type=float, default=0.0) args = ap.parse_args() mp.set_start_method("spawn") q_meta, q_stop = mp.Queue(), mp.Queue() p = mp.Process(target=p_main, args=(args.pgpu, q_meta, q_stop)) p.start() meta, raddr, rgpu = q_meta.get() try: d_main(args, meta, raddr, rgpu) finally: q_stop.put(1) p.join(10) ``` Run: `UCX_NET_DEVICES=all python nixl_add_remove_loop.py --iters 400 --every 50` (add `--no-xfer`, `--no-remove`, `--settle 25` for the other rows). On an RDMA node, also watch `wc -l /proc//maps` and `rdma resource show qp | grep -c "pid "`.
### What needs fixing **NIXL / UCX** - `invalidateRemoteMD` should actually close the UCX endpoints on every worker (and report failure if it cannot), so add/remove is resource-neutral. **vLLM** - Stop treating eviction as free. Until NIXL releases endpoints, `engine_ttl` churn is a per-process countdown; consider defaulting it off or making eviction much rarer. Workaround today: `engine_ttl: 0`. - Related leak on handshake failure: `add_remote_agent` (`base_worker.py:2119`) stores `dst_xfer_side_handles[engine_id][rank]` (`:2384`) and the NIXL remote agent per rank, but `_remote_agents[engine_id]` is only committed in `_ensure_handshake`'s `done_callback` after all ranks succeed. A handshake that fails at rank k leaves ranks 0..k-1 loaded with live dlist handles; the retry re-adds them and overwrites the handles without `release_dlist_handle`. Once a worker is at the wall, every retry pays this. - A metric for remote agents added/removed per worker would have made this visible days earlier. ### Related - #59871 heartbeats do not refresh `engine_ttl` (one trigger of the churn; it notes the buffers left behind as "a separate NIXL/UCX issue", which is this one) - #59872 / #59874 stuck READ strands decode KV blocks - #58063 / #57507 decoder keeps a dead prefill's KV cache mapped via `cuda_ipc` (also reproduced here: `remove_remote_agent` after TTL eviction did not release 23 GiB/GPU of a killed prefill; only decode exit did) - #59870 unsynchronized NIXL agent access This is not a duplicate of the above: none of them cover `remove_remote_agent` leaking endpoints or include a reproducer for it. _AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to investigate and to draft this issue; the reproducer was run and the numbers above are from those runs._

The default `fallback=true` does not help: the disk fallback then fails with `Duplicate layer name`, so the engine cannot start at all. The preload docs list expert parallelism as supported ([`docs/features/preload.md` L26-L28](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/863475eb9cd78ae6a4a22f1b90df7fe85e0af438/docs/features/preload.md#L26-L28), [L167](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/863475eb9cd78ae6a4a22f1b90df7fe85e0af438/docs/features/preload.md#L167)). #### Reproduction Two GPUs, public tiny model, EPLB not enabled. ```bash # Terminal 1 vllm preload --model tiny-random/qwen3-moe --tensor-parallel-size 2 \ --enable-expert-parallel ``` Wait for `Weight cache daemon READY`, then: ```bash # Terminal 2 vllm serve tiny-random/qwen3-moe --tensor-parallel-size 2 \ --enable-expert-parallel --load-format ipc_cache \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.2 ``` `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.2` is there only because the GPUs on my machine are shared. #### Results - With the default `fallback=true`, the engine fails with `ValueError: Duplicate layer name: model.layers.0.self_attn.attn`. - With `--model-loader-extra-config '{"fallback": false}'` added to `vllm serve`, it fails with `NotImplementedError: The register_meta function for torch.nonzero() ...`. #### Cause 1. The IPC loader builds the model under `torch.device("meta")` ([`ipc_loader.py` L259-L264](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/863475eb9cd78ae6a4a22f1b90df7fe85e0af438/vllm/model_executor/model_loader/weight_cache/ipc_loader.py#L259-L264)). 2. With EP on, `ExpertMapManager.__init__` logs the expert map ([`expert_map_manager.py` L248-L261](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/863475eb9cd78ae6a4a22f1b90df7fe85e0af438/vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/expert_map_manager.py#L248-L261)). `get_compressed_map_string()` calls `torch.where(self._expert_map != -1)` ([L409](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/863475eb9cd78ae6a4a22f1b90df7fe85e0af438/vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/expert_map_manager.py#L409)). `_expert_map` is a meta tensor here. `torch.where(cond)` is `torch.nonzero`, which cannot run on meta tensors, so it raises `NotImplementedError`. 3. With `fallback=true`, `load_model` catches the error and calls `_fallback_load` ([`ipc_loader.py` L225-L237](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/863475eb9cd78ae6a4a22f1b90df7fe85e0af438/vllm/model_executor/model_loader/weight_cache/ipc_loader.py#L225-L237)), which builds the model a second time. The first, partial build already registered its first attention layer in `compilation_config.static_forward_context` ([`attention.py` L443-L445](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/863475eb9cd78ae6a4a22f1b90df7fe85e0af438/vllm/model_executor/layers/attention/attention.py#L443-L445)), so the second build raises `Duplicate layer name`. Step 3 does not look specific to EP: from the code, any exception raised inside `_build_model` after the first attention layer is constructed would leave the fallback unable to rebuild the model. I have only observed it through the path above. #### Scope - Tested at `863475eb9c`. The files linked above are unchanged on `main` at `0979892992` (2026-10-02). - Only tested with `tiny-random/qwen3-moe` at TP=2. #### Related PRs - #55490 (open, needs rebase) builds the expert map on the CPU (`_expert_map_cpu`). From reading the diff, this should fix step 2. I have not run it. - #43928 (draft) makes the same log line skip meta tensors, which should also avoid the crash in step 2. I have not run it either. - #58876 (closed, not merged) built the expert map on the host. - None of them changes the fallback path in step 3. #### Note for the fix #55490 also rejects `--enable-eplb` with `ipc_cache`. `main` has no such check, and the crash above is the only thing that stops that combination today, because EPLB requires EP. The check should land together with the fix. With step 2 worked around locally and EPLB on in `zero_copy` mode, EPLB's in-place rearrangement rewrote the daemon's cached expert weights, and the next engine attached to the same daemon produced different outputs with no error. I can share the details if useful. > AI disclosure: this issue was investigated and drafted with an AI assistant (Claude). A human reviewed the issue before filing. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

### 🐛 Describe the bug # [Bug]: CUTLASS fp8 MoE corrupts valid tokens when CUDA-graph padding routes are `-1` (wrong `expert_first_token_offset` from `moe_permute`) ## Your current environment - vLLM **0.29.0** (tag), **0.30.0** (`ced6857afa0e`) and **`main` at `47de9d4d04`** (2026-10-01, precompiled kernels), identical results. - torch 2.13.0+cu130, H100 80GB HBM3 (SM 9.0), TP=1 and TP=2. - V2 model runner, default compilation (`VLLM_COMPILE`, `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` CUDA graphs), `VLLM_MOE_SKIP_PADDING=1` (default). - MoE backend auto-selected as `VLLM_CUTLASS` (`CutlassExpertsFp8`) for a compressed-tensors `FP8_DYNAMIC` checkpoint (per-channel weight scales, per-token dynamic activation scales). ## 🐛 Describe the bug With the CUTLASS fp8 MoE backend, **valid tokens get the wrong MoE output whenever the batch contains padding tokens**. CUDA-graph replay pads small batches up to a capture size, and with `VLLM_MOE_SKIP_PADDING=1` the router writes `topk_ids = -1` for those padding tokens. The CUTLASS path then computes wrong per-expert offsets and runs some real tokens through the wrong expert's weights. User-visible effect (a 128-expert, top-4, fp8 MoE model): with single-request serving the first generated token often collapses (e.g. bf16 `'Yes'` p=0.90 becomes `'\n'` p=0.997 in fp8), and sampled output drifts into unrelated text. The same checkpoint is correct with batched requests, with `--moe-backend triton` or `marlin`, with `--enforce-eager`, with CUDA graphs disabled, or with `VLLM_MOE_SKIP_PADDING=0`. 56-expert and 224-expert fp8 models served the same way are also affected, less often. ### Minimal repro (no weights, a few seconds on one GPU) ```python #!/usr/bin/env python3 """Minimal repro: vLLM moe_permute computes wrong expert_first_token_offset when topk_ids contains -1 (the id the router writes for CUDA-graph padding tokens when VLLM_MOE_SKIP_PADDING=1, the default). No weights needed. The CUTLASS fp8 MoE path (CutlassExpertsFp8) feeds these offsets to the grouped GEMM, so a wrong boundary runs some real tokens through the wrong expert. Run on any CUDA GPU with vLLM installed: python vllm_moe_permute_neg1_repro.py """ import torch from vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe.moe_permute_unpermute import moe_permute E, TOPK, HIDDEN = 128, 4, 256 # 120B-class MoE: 128 experts, top-4 torch.manual_seed(0) bad_cases = bad_remapped = 0 for n_valid in range(1, 49): n_pad = 8 * ((n_valid + 7) // 8) - n_valid # pad to a CUDA-graph size valid = torch.stack([torch.randperm(E)[:TOPK] for _ in range(n_valid)]) topk_ids = torch.cat([valid, torch.full((n_pad, TOPK), -1)]).int().cuda() hidden = torch.randn(n_valid + n_pad, HIDDEN, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16) _, _, offsets, _, _ = moe_permute(hidden, None, topk_ids, E, E, None) counts = torch.bincount(valid.reshape(-1).long(), minlength=E) expected = torch.cat([torch.zeros(1, dtype=torch.long), counts.cumsum(0)]) wrong = (offsets.cpu() != expected).nonzero().reshape(-1).tolist() # same routing with padding routes remapped from -1 to E remapped = torch.where(topk_ids < 0, torch.full_like(topk_ids, E), topk_ids) _, _, offsets_r, _, _ = moe_permute(hidden, None, remapped, E, E, None) bad_remapped += bool((offsets_r.cpu() != expected).any()) if wrong: bad_cases += 1 e = wrong[0] print(f"n_valid={n_valid:2d} n_pad={n_pad}: {len(wrong)} wrong offsets, " f"first at expert {e}: got {offsets[e].item()}, expected {expected[e].item()}") print(f"\n{bad_cases} of 48 batch sizes have wrong expert offsets with -1 padding") print(f"{bad_remapped} of 48 with the padding routes remapped from -1 to E") ``` Output (identical on 0.29.0, 0.30.0 and `main`): ``` n_valid= 1 n_pad=7: 129 wrong offsets, first at expert 0: got 32, expected 0 n_valid= 2 n_pad=6: 129 wrong offsets, first at expert 0: got 32, expected 0 n_valid= 3 n_pad=5: 129 wrong offsets, first at expert 0: got 32, expected 0 n_valid= 4 n_pad=4: 9 wrong offsets, first at expert 120: got 32, expected 16 ... 42 of 48 batch sizes have wrong expert offsets with -1 padding 0 of 48 with the padding routes remapped from -1 to E ``` Every padded batch size is wrong; the 6 correct sizes are the multiples of 8, which have no padding. When padding outnumbers the valid tokens (e.g. `n_valid=1, n_pad=7`), every offset equals the total route count, so every expert segment is empty and the valid tokens' MoE output is silently zero. ### End-to-end op repro (`CutlassExpertsFp8`, random weights, E=128, top-4, K=3072, N=1536) Rows `[0, n)` of the CUTLASS MoE output, compared with the same call on the valid rows alone (relative error), for `n = 1..48` padded to the next vLLM CUDA-graph capture size (1, 2, 4, then multiples of 8): | padding rows | routing | valid-row error | |---|---|---| | 0 | — | 0 in all sizes | | > 0, `topk_ids = -1` | default | **wrong in 25 of 40 sizes** (rel. error 0.09 to 0.94) | | > 0, routed to real experts | `VLLM_MOE_SKIP_PADDING=0` equivalent | 0 in all sizes | | > 0, `-1` remapped to `E` | proposed fix | 0 in all sizes | The same corruption appears with or without CUDA-graph capture, so the graph only matters because it is what produces the padding. The 25 corrupted sizes are exactly the sizes where at least one valid route lands in another expert's segment of the permuted buffer (25/25 corrupted, 0/23 clean). ### Why batched accuracy benchmarks miss it Padding rows only exist when a forward pass runs a CUDA graph whose capture size is larger than its token count. Single-request serving hits this on most prompt prefills: a 27-token prompt runs in the 32-token graph with 5 padding tokens (20 `-1` routes at top-4). Across 180 single-request prompts, sequences whose prefill had 0-3 padding tokens were never affected (0/100); 17/80 with 4-7 padding tokens were. Offline accuracy runs that queue thousands of requests mostly avoid that shape: prefill steps pack well over the 512-token largest capture size (no graph, so no padding), and decode batches are large, so the `-1` tail is a small fraction of the routes. The affected fp8 checkpoint scored within one standard error of its bf16 source on MMLU-Pro (77.8% vs 78.1%, 12,032 questions, sampled with thinking on), while the same checkpoint served one request at a time collapsed as described above. Comparing next-token distributions against the bf16 model with one request per engine call catches it directly: | 128-expert fp8 checkpoint, first 8 response tokens | foreign mass (mean / p99) | top-1 agreement with bf16 | |---|---|---| | one request at a time, greedy (`main`, unpatched) | 0.0081 / 0.39 | 0.951 | | all 180 requests in one batch, teacher-forced | 0.0000 / 0.0000 | 0.990 | "Foreign mass" is the probability the fp8 model puts on its top-10 tokens that are outside the bf16 model's top-100; it is exactly 0 for bf16 against itself. ## Root cause `moe_permute` → `sortAndScanExpert` (`csrc/libtorch_stable/moe/permute_unpermute_kernels/moe_permute_unpermute_kernel.cu`): 1. `CubKeyValueSorter` radix-sorts only the low `expertsToBits(E) = floor(log2(2E-1)) + 1` bits. `-1` is `0xFFFFFFFF`, so its low bits are all ones and padding routes sort **after** every real expert (keys `[0, 0, 1, ..., E-1, -1, -1, ...]`). 2. `computeExpertFirstTokenOffsetKernel` (on `main`: `computeExpertOffsetsAndInverseKernel`) gets each offset from `findTotalEltsLessThanTarget`, a binary search that assumes the keys are ascending as signed ints. The trailing `-1`s break that assumption: whenever a probe lands in the tail, `-1 >= target` is false, the search moves right, and the offset (including the final valid-row count) comes out too large. 3. `run_cutlass_moe_fp8` passes those offsets to `get_cutlass_moe_mm_problem_sizes_from_expert_offsets` / `cutlass_moe_mm`, so an expert's GEMM segment can extend over the next expert's rows. A Python emulation of steps 1 and 2 reproduces the kernel's offsets exactly in 48/48 cases. On `main`, `preprocessTopkIdKernel` already maps ids outside `[0, n_expert)` to `n_expert` (and accepts a null `expert_map`), but `moe_sort_routing` only launches it when `expert_map.has_value() || build_inverse`. `moe_permute` and `moe_permute_with_scratch`, the entry points `CutlassExpertsFp8` uses, pass `build_inverse=false` and no expert map on a single EP rank, so they skip the remap; only `moe_prepare_scatter` (`build_inverse=true`) gets it. The existing `test_moe_permute_ignores_invalid_expert_ids_with_scratch` always passes an `expert_map`, so this path is untested. #54747 ("Handle padded routes in CUTLASS MoE permutations") fixed sentinel handling in `get_cutlass_moe_mm_data` / `shuffle_rows`, but the fp8 path in `run_cutlass_moe_fp8` (non-batched) gets its offsets from `moe_permute`, which still has this problem. ## Workarounds - `VLLM_MOE_SKIP_PADDING=0` (keeps CUTLASS and CUDA graphs; padding tokens get real routes) - `--moe-backend triton` or `marlin` - `--enforce-eager` / `cudagraph_mode=NONE` (slower) ## Proposed fix Always run the existing `preprocessTopkIdLauncher` remap in `moe_sort_routing` (not only with an `expert_map` or `build_inverse`), so invalid ids become the `n_expert` sentinel the sort and offset scan are designed around (`sortAndScanExpert` already notes that `n_expert` is the sentinel for disabled experts). Also make `preprocessTopkIdLauncher` return early for an empty batch, which the unconditional call would otherwise reach with `block = 0`. Tested on `main` `47de9d4d04` by rebuilding `_moe_C_stable_libtorch` (sm_90, CUDA 13.1) with this change: | check | unpatched | patched | |---|---|---| | minimal repro, batch sizes with wrong offsets | 42 / 48 | 0 / 48 | | `CutlassExpertsFp8` end-to-end, sizes with valid-row corruption | 25 / 48 | 0 / 48 | | new test `test_moe_permute_invalid_expert_ids_without_expert_map` (E ∈ {16, 128, 224}, top-k ∈ {4, 8}, 4 padding cases, with/without scratch) | 48 failed | 48 passed | | rest of `tests/kernels/moe/test_moe_permute_unpermute.py` | | 454 passed | I can open a PR with this change and the test. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Searched existing issues; closest are #56900 / #57823 (top-k softmax row stride, a different bug) and #54747 (sentinels in `moe_data.cu`, does not cover `moe_permute` offsets). - Related: other backends have received fixes for the same `-1` padding sentinel (AITER #57036, FlashInfer b12x #57946, XPU #55231, Triton under EP #54083); this is the CUTLASS fp8 / `moe_permute` instance. #58789 / #58790 handle empty routing in `moe_permute`, a separate (zero-row) case. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

items.title: [Bug]: Xid 31 MMU fault under load in multi-node Expert-Parallel (EP16) CUDA-graph replay (fused-MoE FP8 reduce_scatterv) — --enforce-eager clean
items.body:
### Your current environment

<details>
<summary>Environment (click to expand)</summary>

- **vLLM:** `v0.18.0+rhaiv.14` (Red Hat AI build; V1 engine)
- **Model:** `Qwen3-Coder-480B-A35B-Instruct-FP8` (MoE, FP8 **block quantization**, `block_n=128`)
- **GPUs:** 2 nodes × 8× **NVIDIA H200** (16 total); NVLink/NVSwitch intra-node, **RoCE** inter-node
- **Parallelism:** `tensor_parallel_size=8`, `data_parallel_size=2`, `enable_expert_parallel=True` (EP16), `data_parallel_size_local=1`
- **Quantization:** `fp8` (block quant); `kv_cache_dtype=auto`
- **all2all manager:** `AgRsAll2AllManager` (default `all2all_backend=allgather_reducescatter`)
- **Attention backend:** `FLASH_ATTN`
- **Compilation (default):** `CompilationMode.VLLM_COMPILE`, `cudagraph_mode=FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`
- **custom all-reduce:** enabled by default (`disable_custom_all_reduce=False`); crash also occurs with it disabled
- **Serving:** OpenShift AI / KServe `LLMInferenceService` → `LeaderWorkerSet` with `RecreateGroupOnPodRestart` (any worker death tears down + recreates the whole 16-GPU group)

> **EP cannot be disabled for this model.** With `expert=false` the MoE FFN weights get TP8-sharded and the per-shard output size (160) isn't divisible by the FP8 block-quant block (128):
> `ValueError: output_size ... = 160 is not divisible by weight quantization block_n = 128`.
> So EP is mandatory; the only test lever is the EP all-to-all **transport/execution**, not EP on/off.
</details>

### 🐛 Describe the bug

Serving **Qwen3-Coder-480B-A35B-Instruct-FP8** (MoE) across **2 nodes / 16× H200** (TP8 · DP2 · EP16, RoCE), the engine **crashes with a GPU Xid 31 MMU page fault** within tens of requests under moderate concurrent load.

The fault is **deterministically tied to CUDA-graph-captured execution of the expert-parallel collective path**:

- reproduces with `cudagraph_mode=FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` **and** `cudagraph_mode=PIECEWISE`
- **completely disappears with `--enforce-eager`** (cudagraphs off) — 400/400 clean, 16h+ healthy

We have ruled out **hardware**, the **custom all-reduce** kernel, and the **all2all backend choice**. This looks like a cudagraph capture/replay correctness bug in the fused-MoE FP8 + EP `reduce_scatterv` combine path.

#### Reproduction

1. Deploy the model multi-node 16-GPU: TP8 / DP2 / EP16, RoCE, **default** `allgather_reducescatter` backend, cudagraphs **ON** (default).
2. Drive load:
   ```bash
   vllm bench serve --backend openai-chat --endpoint /v1/chat/completions \
     --model <name> --dataset-name random \
     --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 512 --random-range-ratio 0.5 --ignore-eos \
     --max-concurrency 16 --num-prompts 400 --request-rate inf
   ```
3. Within ~30 requests the engine dies; LWS recreates the 16-GPU group (~8 min outage). Also reproduced at `--max-concurrency 8` (crash at the tail of the run). **Halving concurrency does not prevent it** → not a simple capacity/concurrency limit.

Performance is **within SLA right up to the fault** (ITL p50 ~25 ms, TPOT p50 ~34 ms, TTFT p50 ~315 ms) — this is a stability crash, not a saturation/queueing failure.

#### The fault

**GPU driver (authoritative, survives pod recreate) — `dmesg`:**
```text
NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:1b:00): 31, pid=..., name=VLLM::Worker, channel 0x0000000c,
  MMU Fault: ENGINE GRAPHICS GPC1 GPCCLIENT_T1_x faulted @ 0x....
  Fault is of type FAULT_PDE ACCESS_TYPE_VIRT_READ
```
Always on the **rank-0 / TP-0 / EP-0** worker's GPU. Same signature every time (Xid 31, GRAPHICS GPC1, `FAULT_PDE ACCESS_TYPE_VIRT_READ`).

**vLLM traceback (captured live before group recreate) — rank-0 worker (`Worker_DP0_TP0_EP0`).** The illegal access surfaces inside a **PIECEWISE CUDA-graph replay** of the Qwen3 MoE forward, in the **EP combine** collective (condensed; full trace in the collapsible block below):
```text
gpu_model_runner.py:3348 _model_forward
qwen3_moe.py:768 forward
compilation/decorators.py:452 __call__ (aot_compiled_fn)
<eval_with_key>.280:813 forward (submod_70)
compilation/cuda_graph.py:251 __call__
compilation/piecewise_backend.py:377 __call__ (range_entry.runnable)
<inductor graph>  torchinductor_.../c2rna...py:1133 call
torch.ops.vllm.moe_forward.default(buf7, buf8, None, 'from_forward_context')
fused_moe/runner/default_moe_runner.py:85 _moe_forward -> :693 forward_impl
quantization/fp8.py:992 apply -> moe_kernel.apply
fused_moe/modular_kernel.py:1581 apply -> :1381 apply -> :1256 _finalize
fused_moe/prepare_finalize/naive_dp_ep.py:164 finalize
get_ep_group().combine(...)                     # parallel_state.py:1114
cuda_communicator.py:482 combine -> all2all.py:245 combine
dist_group.reduce_scatterv(hidden_states, dim=0, sizes=sizes)
cuda_communicator.py:292 reduce_scatterv
pynccl.py:311 reduce_scatterv -> pynccl_wrapper.py:457 ncclReduce
RuntimeError: NCCL error: unhandled cuda error (run with NCCL_DEBUG=INFO for details)
```
The illegal access then re-raises as `torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered`, which the engine core reports as `EngineDeadError` across all API-server ranks.
On the other API-server/worker ranks the same corruption surfaces downstream as:
```text
Cuda error .../csrc/custom_all_reduce.cuh:621 'an illegal memory access was encountered'
-> vllm.v1.engine.exceptions.EngineDeadError
```
i.e. the MMU fault corrupts the CUDA context on rank-0 (in the EP `reduce_scatterv` combine during graph replay); NCCL then reports "unhandled cuda error" and the custom all-reduce on peers reports the illegal access. **The custom-all-reduce message is a downstream symptom, not the cause** (crash reproduces with custom all-reduce disabled).

#### What we ruled out, and how

| Hypothesis | Experiment | Result |
|---|---|---|
| **Faulty GPU (silicon)** | `dcgmi diag -r 1/3/4` (memtest, pulse, nvbandwidth, pcie, targeted_stress), ECC aggregate, row-remap, NVLink counters on the faulting GPU | **All clean / Pass**, ECC all 0, no row-remap pending |
| **Faulty GPU (silicon)** | Run model **single-node 8-GPU (TP8/EP8)** pinned to each node under identical load | **Both nodes 400/400, 0 Xid** — the "always 1B:00" GPU handled the load cleanly |
| **Faulty GPU (silicon)** | **Leader-swap:** force rank-0 onto the *other* node's GPU0 (different UUID/serial), same load | **Xid 31 moved with rank-0** to the different physical card; old card (now worker) stayed clean → **fault follows the RANK, not the silicon** |
| **Custom all-reduce** | `--disable-custom-all-reduce` (`disable_custom_all_reduce=True` confirmed in engine) | **Still crashes**, identical Xid 31 |
| **EP all2all backend** | `--all2all-backend naive` | Non-viable: worker dies during FULL cudagraph capture (never reaches Ready) |
| **EP all2all backend** | `--all2all-backend deepep_low_latency` | Non-viable: **Xid 43** (kernel launch fail) on all 16 GPUs at KV-cache profiling |
| **CUDA-graph FULL decode graph** | `cudagraph_mode=PIECEWISE` (drop FULL pass) | **Still crashes**, identical Xid 31 |
| **CUDA graphs at all** | `--enforce-eager` (`cudagraph_mode=NONE`) | **400/400 SUCCESS, 0 failed, 0 Xid, engine healthy 16h+** |

**Decisive evidence**

- **Hardware excluded:** fault follows rank-0 across *different physical GPUs* (leader-swap); single-node runs on the "suspect" GPU are 400/400 clean; DCGM / ECC / NVLink all clean.
- **CUDA graphs are the trigger:** the *only* configuration change that eliminates the crash is turning cudagraphs off (`--enforce-eager`). `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` crashes, `PIECEWISE` crashes, `NONE` is clean.
- **Not the custom all-reduce** (crashes on and off) and **not backend math** (eager uses the same kernels and is clean).

#### Suspected root cause

A CUDA-graph capture/replay correctness bug in the **multi-node expert-parallel path** — specifically the fused-MoE FP8 modular kernel combine that performs a variable-size `reduce_scatterv` (`AgRsAll2AllManager.combine` → pynccl `ncclReduce`) inside a piecewise graph. Under concurrent/variable-shape load the replayed graph appears to issue a GPU memory access with a stale/invalid address (MMU `FAULT_PDE ACCESS_TYPE_VIRT_READ` in the GRAPHICS engine), corrupting the context; NCCL and the custom all-reduce then report secondary errors.

Candidate areas: captured buffers/pointers in the EP combine for dynamic `sizes=`; interaction of `reduce_scatterv` with graph capture; or the FP8 grouped-GEMM MoE path under piecewise inductor partitioning (NCCL collective not honored by `splitting_ops`).

#### Workaround

`--enforce-eager` eliminates the crash but costs throughput/latency:

- eager: **TPOT ~80 ms, ITL ~80 ms, TTFT ~272 ms, ~583 tok/s** @ conc 16 (400/400 clean)
- vs cudagraph single-node: TPOT ~16 ms, ITL ~15 ms

Eager misses our 30–50 ms TPOT target, so it's a functional stopgap, not a performance-acceptable fix. `cudagraph_mode=PIECEWISE` is **not** a usable middle ground (still crashes).

#### Related issues

Not an exact duplicate of any of these, but they form a clear cluster — each matches one axis of this crash:

- **#46253** — *Cross-node piecewise-cudagraph capture → illegal memory access; NCCL collective captured, `splitting_ops` not honored; `--enforce-eager` fixes.* **Closest root-cause thesis.** Differs: theirs faults at **capture** (GB-class, host-staged NCCL); ours faults at **replay** under load on H200 with working RoCE.
- **#58850** — *Intermittent Xid 31 MMU fault in pynccl collective during CUDA graph.* **Closest fault signature** (identical Xid 31 / GRAPHICS GPC / pynccl / CUDA graph). Differs: theirs is intermittent at capture on a TP all-reduce (dense); ours is deterministic at replay in the EP MoE combine.
- **#59189** — *EP serving crashes in NCCL reduce-scatter (EP combine → `reduce_scatterv` → NCCL "unhandled cuda error") under high concurrency.* **Closest stack surface.** Differs: theirs requires `VLLM_USE_NCCL_SYMM_MEM=1` (symmetric-memory scratch regression, bisected to #48247) and is **not** cudagraph-triggered; ours is plain pynccl `ncclReduce` and **is** cudagraph-triggered.

**How this report is distinct:** deterministic at **replay under load** (not capture); EP MoE combine via plain pynccl `reduce_scatterv` (not symm-mem); **Xid 31**; `--enforce-eager` clean; on **H200 / RoCE**; both `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` and `PIECEWISE` crash.

#### Questions / asks for triage

- [ ] Is the EP `reduce_scatterv`/all2all combine (`AgRsAll2AllManager`) expected to be CUDA-graph-safe for **variable `sizes=`** across replays? If not, should it be added to `splitting_ops` / excluded from capture for EP?
- [ ] Any known fixes post-`v0.18.0+rhaiv.14` touching fused-MoE modular kernel + cudagraph + EP combine?
- [ ] We can collect `NCCL_DEBUG=INFO`, `compute-sanitizer` (memcheck) on rank-0, and a reduced-`cudagraph_capture_sizes` run if helpful — let us know what's most useful.

<details>
<summary>Full rank-0 worker traceback (cudagraph replay → EP combine → reduce_scatterv → ncclReduce → NCCL error) — PIECEWISE run, 2026-10-01 11:28:12</summary>

### 🐛 Describe the bug ## Description On H100 (SM90) vLLM v0.30.0's FA4 forward kernel ignores `num_splits`, so decode attention always runs as a single KV split. Models with few KV heads lose most of their decode attention parallelism. For [google/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it](https://huggingface.co/google/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it) at ~6k context, a decode step is **48% slower** than on v0.26.0 at batch 1 and **36% slower** at batch 4. Results stay correct (the empty splits are weighted at zero) so nothing fails but it's just slow. The one-line fix was merged in the fork on 2026-09-28 as [vllm-project/flash-attention#198](https://github.com/vllm-project/flash-attention/pull/198) (`6d11b3c`) but vLLM hasn't picked it up yet. The regression came in with the pin move in #54819: | vLLM | `vllm_flash_attn` pin | Has the fix? | |---|---|---| | v0.26.0 to v0.29.0 | `caaa4eb` ... `06bdd47` | Not needed, bug not present | | v0.30.0 | `506341a` (#54819) | **No** | | main | `9cd61de` | **No** (one commit behind `6d11b3c`) | **Ask:** bump the `GIT_TAG` in `cmake/external_projects/vllm_flash_attn.cmake` to `6d11b3c` or later, and backport it to a v0.30.x patch release if there is one. The fix was validated at the kernel level and this issue adds end-to-end numbers on v0.30.0 below. ## Root Cause Analysis We isolated it one component at a time on v0.30.0, starting from the end-to-end decode slowdown: | Step | What we changed | Result | Conclusion | |---|---|---|---| | 1 | Split time to first token from per-token decode | Decode +48% per token, TTFT flat (61 ms on both) | Decode only | | 2 | Batch 4 → 1 | Gap *grows* (+36% → +48%) | Not batching or scheduler contention | | 3 | V1 v/s V2 model runner, text-only prompts, same MoE configs | V1 runner: +49% (bs 1), +34% (bs 4) | Not the runner, multimodal or MoE | | 4 | Context ~260 → ~5.9k tokens | v0.26 flat (4.34 → 4.38 ms), v0.30 +8% → +48% | Scales with KV length: attention | | 5 | `attention_backend=TRITON_ATTN` on v0.30 | Recovers ~70% of the gap | The problem is in FA4 | | 6 | torch.profiler per-kernel diff, bs 1, ~5.9k context | Attention 0.53 → 2.51 ms/step; GEMM, MoE, norms flat | One kernel | | 7 | Kernel alone, sweep `num_splits` | v0.26: 374 → 20 µs with more splits. v0.30: flat 348-364 µs | `num_splits` is ignored | In step 6 the global-layer FA4 kernel goes from 18.5 µs to 311 µs per launch with an **identical** launch configuration (grid `[2, 66, 1]`, 384 threads, 205,824 B shared memory). The same CTAs launch, but only one split per head has work, which is why this doesn't show up in a launch-config diff. ### Mechanism The fork sync that v0.30.0 pins (`506341a`) moved the split count into a `BlockInfo` field. `BlockInfo.get_n_block_min_max` in `vllm_flash_attn/cute/block_info.py` still takes `num_splits` as an argument but overwrites it on the non-packed path: ```python if cutlass.const_expr(self.is_split_kv): if const_expr(self.pack_split_idx): num_splits = split_idx >> 16 # SM100: packed into split_idx else: num_splits = self.num_splits # SM90: the constructor value, default Int32(1) ``` `flash_fwd_sm100.py` constructs `BlockInfo(..., num_splits=num_splits)` but `flash_fwd_sm90.py` doesn't, so on SM90 split 0 covers the whole KV range and splits 1..N-1 get `n_block_min == n_block_max`. The combine kernel weights the empty splits at zero so results are correct. Gemma-4's global layers are the worst case: 1 query token and 2 KV heads per sequence, so without splits only 2 of the H100's 132 SMs have work. The fix ([vllm-project/flash-attention#198](https://github.com/vllm-project/flash-attention/pull/198)): ```diff --- a/flash_attn/cute/flash_fwd_sm90.py +++ b/flash_attn/cute/flash_fwd_sm90.py @@ -686,6 +686,7 @@ def kernel( window_size_left, window_size_right, qhead_per_kvhead_packgqa=self.qhead_per_kvhead if const_expr(self.pack_gqa) else 1, + num_splits=num_splits, ) ``` ## Reproduction
Environment * vLLM: 0.30.0 (bug), 0.26.0 (reference), official `vllm/vllm-openai` images, CUDA 13.0 * PyTorch: 2.13.0+cu130 (v0.30.0), 2.11.0+cu130 (v0.26.0) * CuTe DSL (`nvidia-cutlass-dsl`): 4.7.1 (v0.30.0), 4.6.0 (v0.26.0) * GPU: 1x H100 80GB HBM3 (p5.48xlarge)
Model * [google/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it](https://huggingface.co/google/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it): 30 layers, 25 sliding-window (head dim 256, 8 KV heads, window 1024) and 5 global (head dim 512, 2 KV heads) with 16 query heads.
Configuration Same engine arguments on both versions, via `vllm.LLM(...)` (the text-only decode numbers below): ```python tensor_parallel_size=1, quantization="fp8", attention_backend="FLASH_ATTN", # v0.30.0; v0.26.0 selects FLASH_ATTN on its own max_model_len=8192, max_num_seqs=8, max_num_batched_tokens=14000, gpu_memory_utilization=0.9, enforce_eager=False, # cudagraph_mode resolves to FULL_AND_PIECEWISE (the default) on both versions trust_remote_code=True, limit_mm_per_prompt={"video": 0, "audio": 0}, mm_processor_cache_gb=8, disable_custom_all_reduce=True, # no-op at TP=1 ``` Prefix caching, chunked prefill and async scheduling are at their defaults. v0.30.0 uses the V2 model runner (its default) but the V1 runner (`VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0`) shows the same slowdown.
Minimum Script to Reproduce Kernel only, no model needed. Paged decode at Gemma-4 global-layer shapes, sweeping `num_splits`: ```python import torch from vllm.vllm_flash_attn import flash_attn_varlen_func SEQK, PAGE, HD, NQ, NKV, BS = 7040, 32, 512, 16, 2, 1 nblk = (SEQK + PAGE - 1) // PAGE k = torch.randn(BS * nblk, PAGE, NKV, HD, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda") v = torch.randn_like(k) q = torch.randn(BS, NQ, HD, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda") bt = torch.arange(BS * nblk, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda").view(BS, nblk) cu_q = torch.arange(BS + 1, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda") sk = torch.full((BS,), SEQK, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda") for ns in (1, 4, 16, 64): f = lambda: flash_attn_varlen_func(q=q, k=k, v=v, max_seqlen_q=1, cu_seqlens_q=cu_q, max_seqlen_k=SEQK, seqused_k=sk, block_table=bt, causal=True, softmax_scale=1.0, num_splits=ns, fa_version=4) for _ in range(3): f() g = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph() with torch.cuda.graph(g): for _ in range(20): f() s, e = torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True), torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True) s.record(); [g.replay() for _ in range(10)]; e.record(); torch.cuda.synchronize() print(f"num_splits={ns}: {s.elapsed_time(e) / 200 * 1e3:.1f} us") ``` Output on one H100 (µs per call), each column run in the `vllm/vllm-openai` image for that version, with the fix mounted over `flash_fwd_sm90.py` for the last one: | `num_splits` | v0.26.0 | v0.30.0 | v0.30.0 + fix | |---|---|---|---| | 1 | 385.4 | 360.1 | 358.6 | | 4 | 104.7 | 360.2 | 101.1 | | 16 | 33.0 | 356.5 | 32.7 | | 64 | 20.3 | 363.0 | 20.2 | The CuTe DSL `UserWarning` about `aux_data` that all three versions print on the first compile is unrelated.
Results Kernel µs per call (CUDA-graph replay, includes the combine kernel) with 7040 KV tokens and 32 page size are shown below. Max error v/s an fp32 reference is identical across all three columns: | Shape | `num_splits` | v0.26.0 | v0.30.0 | v0.30.0 + fix | |---|---|---|---|---| | hd 512, 2 KV heads, bs 1 | 0 (heuristic) | 19.8 | 364.0 | 20.7 | | hd 512, 2 KV heads, bs 1 | 1 | 374.3 | 356.8 | 351.6 | | hd 512, 2 KV heads, bs 1 | 16 | 32.8 | 348.5 | 32.8 | | hd 512, 2 KV heads, bs 1 | 64 | 20.3 | 362.4 | 20.3 | | hd 512, 2 KV heads, bs 4 | 0 (heuristic) | 53.3 | 387.6 | 51.7 | | hd 256, 8 KV heads, window 1024, bs 1 | 0 (heuristic) | 12.3 | 34.5 | 12.2 | End to end: google/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it, text-only greedy decode, ms per step (median of 3): | Context | Batch | v0.26.0 | v0.30.0 | v0.30.0 + fix | |---|---|---|---|---| | ~260 tokens | 1 | 4.335 | 4.691 (+8.2%) | 4.349 (+0.3%) | | ~260 tokens | 4 | 5.179 | 5.558 (+7.3%) | 5.382 (+3.9%) | | ~5.9k tokens | 1 | 4.378 | 6.460 (+47.5%) | 4.440 (+1.4%) | | ~5.9k tokens | 4 | 5.462 | 7.455 (+36.5%) | 5.568 (+1.9%) |
What Works * v0.30.0 + fix (mounted over `vllm_flash_attn/cute/flash_fwd_sm90.py`, no rebuild as it's a JIT kernel): decode within 0.3-3.9% of v0.26.0, of which ~1.5% is the unrelated QK-norm + RoPE change below. * `attention_backend=TRITON_ATTN` on v0.30.0: recovers ~70% of the gap.
What Doesn't Work * Passing `num_splits` explicitly: ignored on SM90 (flat timings above). * V1 model runner (`VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0`): same slowdown.
What Was Ruled Out | Hypothesis | How tested | Result | |---|---|---| | V2 model runner | V1 runner on v0.30.0 | Same slowdown | | Multimodal / structured output | Text-only prompts, no schema | Same slowdown | | MoE kernel / tuning configs | Per-kernel profile; config files diffed | MoE flat, configs identical | | Scheduler / async scheduling | Batch 4 → 1 | Gap grows | | Launch configuration | Grid, threads, smem from the profile | Identical across versions | | torch 2.13 fused QK-norm + RoPE | Per-kernel profile | Real but small (~1.5% of a step), unrelated |
## Related Issues * [vllm-project/flash-attention#198](https://github.com/vllm-project/flash-attention/pull/198): the fix, merged 2026-09-28. * #54819: the pin move (`06bdd47` → `506341a`, fork sync vllm-project/flash-attention#188) that introduced it. * #57680: a different 0.26 → 0.29 decode drop, root-caused to the V2 model runner on Confidential Computing VMs. Not this bug (v0.29.0 doesn't have `506341a`, and our V1-runner control is just as slow). * The same fork sync also kept the pre-[Dao-AILab#2624](https://github.com/Dao-AILab/flash-attention/pull/2624) `seqlen_k_loaded` expression in `flash_attn/cute/interface.py` (`window_size_right or max_seqlen_k` treats a causal window's right bound of 0 as unbounded, so the split heuristic sizes sliding-window layers by the full KV length). No measurable cost at Gemma-4's shapes; worth cherry-picking while bumping the pin. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

items.title: [Bug]: FilesystemResolver loads adapters outside VLLM_LORA_RESOLVER_CACHE_DIR (path traversal via LoRA name)
items.body:
### Your current environment
The output of python collect_env.py ```text OS: Debian GNU/Linux 13.7 (trixie), x86_64, running under WSL2 Kernel: Linux 6.6.87.2-microsoft-standard-WSL2 glibc: 2.41 Python: 3.12.14 NumPy: 2.5.3 PyTorch: 2.13.0+cpu CUDA available: No vLLM package: Not installed; validation executed relevant code extracted from the vLLM v0.30.0 tag ```
### 🐛 Describe the bug Summary `FilesystemResolver.resolve_lora` builds the adapter path with a bare `os.path.join(self.lora_cache_dir, lora_name)` and never checks that the result stays inside the cache directory. A `lora_name` containing `..`, or an absolute path (which makes `os.path.join` discard the cache dir entirely), resolves to a directory anywhere on the server filesystem. `lora_name` is the client-supplied `model` field of an OpenAI API request (`vllm/entrypoints/openai/models/serving.py:304`), so the `VLLM_LORA_RESOLVER_CACHE_DIR` confinement is trivially bypassable. Reproducing the Bug ```python import asyncio import json import os import tempfile from vllm.lora.resolver import LoRAResolverRegistry from vllm.plugins.lora_resolvers.filesystem_resolver import register_filesystem_resolver root = tempfile.mkdtemp() cache_dir = os.path.join(root, "lora_cache") outside = os.path.join(root, "private_adapter") os.makedirs(cache_dir) os.makedirs(outside) with open(os.path.join(outside, "adapter_config.json"), "w") as f: json.dump( {"peft_type": "LORA", "base_model_name_or_path": "meta-llama/Llama-3-8B"}, f ) os.environ["VLLM_LORA_RESOLVER_CACHE_DIR"] = cache_dir register_filesystem_resolver() resolver = LoRAResolverRegistry.get_resolver("Filesystem Resolver") for name in ["../private_adapter", outside]: req = asyncio.run(resolver.resolve_lora("meta-llama/Llama-3-8B", name)) print(name, "->", req.lora_path if req else None) ``` ``` ../private_adapter -> /tmp/tmpXXXX/lora_cache/../private_adapter /tmp/tmpXXXX/private_adapter -> /tmp/tmpXXXX/private_adapter ``` Fix Normalize the joined path and reject anything that does not remain under the cache directory. ```diff --- a/vllm/plugins/lora_resolvers/filesystem_resolver.py +++ b/vllm/plugins/lora_resolvers/filesystem_resolver.py @@ async def resolve_lora( self, base_model_name: str, lora_name: str ) -> LoRARequest | None: - lora_path = os.path.join(self.lora_cache_dir, lora_name) + cache_root = os.path.realpath(self.lora_cache_dir) + lora_path = os.path.realpath(os.path.join(cache_root, lora_name)) + if os.path.commonpath([cache_root, lora_path]) != cache_root or ( + lora_path == cache_root + ): + return None maybe_lora_request = await self._get_lora_req_from_path( lora_name, lora_path, base_model_name ) return maybe_lora_request ``` ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.
