items.title: [Bug][ROCm] v0.30.0: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash cannot boot on gfx942 — Engram pinned-host CPU offload lost on the AMD path (+47 GiB/rank GPU), OOM in profile_run
items.body:
### Your current environment

```
vLLM Version                 : 0.30.0
Image                        : vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:v0.30.0 (official, digest sha256:2e7da1ad1c66…, no custom layers)
PyTorch version              : 2.12.0+git6bbd260
ROCm Version (image)         : 7.2.3 (/opt/rocm-7.2.3, bundled); host user space: ROCm 7.2.4
GPU                          : 8x AMD Instinct MI308X (gfx942, 191.98 GiB each), TP=4 (DeepSeek on GPUs 0-3)
Orchestrator                 : GPUStack v2.2.3 (docker backend)
Model                        : deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash — DeepseekV41ForCausalLM,
                               FP8 (ue8m0) attention + MXFP4 experts, 48 shards / 475.25 GiB,
                               engram_num_embeddings=[384006168, 384016682], head_dim=256
Working image (baseline)     : vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-eed1f3d0c6043bd494424a22443ee198dd56f657
                               (vLLM 0.1.1.dev50+geed1f3d0c, 0.29.x nightly, ~2026-09-12)
<!-- run `vllm collect-env` in the serving container and paste the full output here -->
```

Serve command (production):

```
vllm serve /models/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --served-model-name deepseek-v4.1-flash \
  --tokenizer-mode=deepseek_v41 --tensor-parallel-size=4 --gpu-memory-utilization=0.94 \
  --moe-backend=aiter_triton_mxfp4_bf16 --tool-call-parser=deepseek_v41 \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice --reasoning-parser=deepseek_v41 --mm-encoder-tp-mode=data \
  --max-model-len 819200 --max-num-seqs 32 \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":5,"draft_sample_method":"probabilistic","rejection_sample_method":"block","enable_adaptive_verification":false}'
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1 VLLM_MXFP8_EMULATION_DEQUANT_AT_LOAD=1
VLLM_DEEP_GEMM_WARMUP=skip VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1 VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1
```

### 🐛 Describe the bug

Every startup on v0.30.0 dies in `profile_run` (~2.5 min into init) on all TP workers, and the server never becomes healthy:

```
File ".../vllm/v1/worker/gpu_worker.py", line 572, in determine_available_memory
  self.model_runner.profile_run()
File ".../vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py", line 955, in profile_run
...
File ".../vllm/models/deepseek_v41/amd/vl_model.py", line 309, in forward
File ".../vllm/models/deepseek_v41/amd/model.py", line 1077, in forward
File ".../vllm/v1/attention/ops/rocm_aiter_mla_sparse.py", line 1045, in rocm_aiter_sparse_attn_indexer
  workspace_manager.get_simultaneous(((decode_rows, max_model_len), torch.float32))
File ".../vllm/v1/worker/workspace.py", line 207, in _ensure_workspace_size
  self._current_workspaces[workspace_id] = torch.empty(...)
torch.OutOfMemoryError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 50.00 GiB.
GPU 0 has a total capacity of 191.98 GiB of which 37.10 GiB is free.
Of the allocated memory 150.30 GiB is allocated by PyTorch ...
```

(The same model + same args start fine on the 0.29.x nightly image above the same GPUs.)

### Root cause (code-level, both images inspected)

Two facts combine:

1. **0.30.0 lost the Engram pinned-host CPU offload on the AMD/common path.**
   On the 0.29 nightly, `vllm/models/deepseek_v4_1/common/engram.py:914` wired
   `cpu_offload=engram_config.cpu_offload if engram_config else True` into the
   `ParallelEngramEmbedding`, so the two DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash Engram tables
   (94.4 GiB each; 23.60 GiB per rank at TP4) lived in pinned host memory and were
   read via UVA — each rank's log shows
   `Engram table offloaded to pinned host memory: 9600xxxx rows x 256, 23.60 GiB per rank`,
   and `Model loading took 100.09 GiB` per rank.

   In v0.30.0 the tree was renamed `deepseek_v4_1` → `deepseek_v41`. The NVIDIA path
   still reads the config (`vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/engram.py:358-365`,
   `get_current_vllm_config().engram_config`), but the AMD model instantiates the
   common `Engram` (`vllm/models/deepseek_v41/amd/model.py:64`), whose
   `ParallelEngramEmbedding._allocate_weights()` (`vllm/models/deepseek_v41/common/engram.py:695`)
   now allocates unconditionally on the current (CUDA) device — the `cpu_offload`
   wiring is gone from this path entirely. `EngramConfig.cpu_offload` still defaults
   to `envs.VLLM_PLE_CPU_OFFLOAD` = `True` in 0.30.0, and
   `VllmConfig._resolve_and_verify_engram_config()` even auto-creates the config for
   models with Engram layers — the AMD path just never consults it.

   Result: `Model loading took 147.3 GiB` per rank (+47.2 GiB = exactly 2 x 23.60 GiB),
   no offload log lines.

2. **The profile-time sparse-indexer workspace reservation is unchanged and large.**
   `rocm_aiter_mla_sparse.py` (profiling early-exit branch) reserves a decode-logits
   workspace of `(decode_rows, max_model_len)` fp32. `_max_decode_logits_rows()` would
   bound it to `max_num_seqs * (1 + num_speculative_tokens)` = 192 rows (592 MiB), but
   that bound requires `get_current_vllm_config()`, which is not set during `profile_run`
   in either version — so both images fall back to `num_batched_tokens` = 16384 rows:
   16384 x 819200 x 4 B = **50.00 GiB**.

   On the nightly this 50 GiB reservation succeeds (weights 100.09 GiB → ~80 GiB free)
   and the engine starts (`Available KV cache memory: 11.29 GiB`). On 0.30.0 with
   GPU-resident Engram tables only 37.10 GiB is free → the allocation OOMs and the
   engine core dies.

### Fix

Restore the nightly default on the common/AMD path — one small patch to
`vllm/models/deepseek_v41/common/engram.py::_allocate_weights()`:

```python
cpu_offload = True
try:
    engram_config = get_current_vllm_config().engram_config
    if engram_config is not None:
        cpu_offload = engram_config.cpu_offload
except Exception:
    pass
kwargs = {"device": "cpu", "pin_memory": True} if cpu_offload else {}
```

(also guarding with `is_uva_available()` like the NVIDIA path, and re-adding the
`Engram table offloaded to pinned host memory` log line).

With only this change, v0.30.0 boots identically to the 0.29 nightly on the same rig:

| | 0.29 nightly | v0.30.0 + engram patch |
|---|---|---|
| Engram offload log | 23.60 GiB per rank x8 | 23.60 GiB per rank x8 |
| Model loading | 100.09 GiB/rank | 100.09 GiB/rank |
| Available KV cache | 11.29 GiB (4,031,384 tokens, 4.92x concurrency) | 11.33 GiB (4,045,600 tokens, 4.94x) |
| init engine | 286.43 s | 280.38 s |
| Short request (17*23) | — | `391` correct |
| 30,060-token needle (chunked prefill) | — | exact recall |

### Suggested upstream fix

Make `ParallelEngramEmbedding._allocate_weights()` in
`vllm/models/deepseek_v41/common/engram.py` honor
`vllm_config.engram_config.cpu_offload` (with the `EngramConfig` default, i.e.
`envs.VLLM_PLE_CPU_OFFLOAD` / `True`), matching the NVIDIA variant
(`deepseek_v41/nvidia/engram.py`) and the pre-refactor behavior
(`deepseek_v4_1/common/engram.py:914`). Otherwise every ROCm deployment of
DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash at TP4 on 192 GB GPUs cannot boot on 0.30.0.

Side note: the profile-time fallback in `_max_decode_logits_rows()` means the 50 GiB
decode-logits workspace is reserved and locked even on healthy boots, which is why
TP4 MI308X ends up with only ~11 GiB of KV cache at `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.94`.
The config-based tight bound (192 rows) would presumably be used if
`get_current_vllm_config()` were reachable during profiling — worth a look, though it
is orthogonal to this regression.

Related: #58310 (documents that `cpu_offload=True` is the intended default for these
tables; sizes match our measurements), #58808 (notes `VLLM_PLE_CPU_OFFLOAD` churn),
#58782 (unrelated ROCm DSv4.1 Quark-checkpoint fixes).

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

On pinned vLLM commit `153242a314153637999eb6ebe8dd830e63433bb6`
(`0.30.1rc0+precompiled`), Qwen3-4B greedy serving can produce a different
*first* token when V2 speculative decoding is enabled. In the selected
row-46 replay, ordinary autoregressive serving emits token ID 334; serving
with a seven-token DFlash2 or DSpark drafter emits 95456. The client sends
requests sequentially (concurrency 1). The divergence occurs during the
initial target prefill, before a draft token or rejection decision exists.

Configuration: Qwen3-4B target, matching custom Qwen3-4B drafters, BF16,
flash-attn, tensor parallel size 1, prefix caching enabled, max model length
4096, max batched tokens 32768, max sequences 32, greedy sampling,
`ignore_eos`, 128 output tokens. Both services receive the same preceding
46 requests in the same order before the selected row-46 request. Exact
launch commands and checkpoint hashes were saved in the run provenance.

The selected prompt is:

> **Blueprint for Serverless Computing with AWS Lambda and API Gateway for Blockchain Administration on AWS**
>
> ---
>
> ## **1. Introduction**
>
> This blueprint outlines a comprehensive, secure, and scalable architecture
> for managing a blockchain system using **AWS Lambda** and **API Gateway**,
> leveraging the robust infrastructure of **Amazon Web Services (AWS)**.
> The system is designed to support the administration of a blockchain
> network, ensuring **seamless node communication**, **data integrity**,
> **security**, and **high throughput**. The architecture is built with a
> **stratified analytical methodology**, considering the interplay of
> components and their potential impacts on system performance and security.
>
> ---

This prompt alone is **not** a standalone reproducer: the previous requests
establish the saved serving state, and the two drafter checkpoints are custom.
I can provide the exact ordered requests, checkpoint access, launch commands
and provenance if suitable for a public reproduction.

What we isolated:

- The original AR and DFlash2 AOT artifacts use the same source for three
  fused RMSNorm variants, but select different reduction-block settings.
- A control that only changes the selected prefill dispatch/padding keeps
  the original token IDs and returned scores.
- A prefill-only intervention that aligns those RMSNorm launch settings to
  AR makes all 36 layers' prompt K/V, the selected hidden state and all raw
  prefill logits bitwise equal to AR. DFlash2 then emits all 128 original AR
  token IDs in three fresh-server repetitions, beginning with 334.
- The corresponding DSpark intervention also needs its Q/K RMSNorm+RoPE
  launch configuration aligned to obtain bitwise-equal prefill state. It
  restores the first token to 334, although its later output still diverges.
- Probe-off / probe-on / probe-off runs agree on token IDs, returned scores
  and finish reasons within each condition. The arithmetic intervention is
  deliberately output-changing; the passive capture controls preserve the
  original output.

This establishes a case-specific numerical cause in prefill compilation /
autotuning. It does not establish a production fix, full-heldout agreement,
or a performance result. The installed vLLM runner and rejection sampler
were not edited for these experiments. The pinned checkout had a pre-existing
dirty change in speculative configuration/scheduling; that patch is retained
in provenance.

A separate decode case prevents misdiagnosing this as a rejection-sampler
failure. At a reached row-5 replacement slot, independent AR token A and
submitted draft D are both 334, while the speculative target chooses V=3786
and emits E=3786. The recorded target logits differ, and the rejection
decision is consistent with those logits. Thus `D=A, E!=D` alone does not
imply a verifier bug. Likewise, later output divergence alone does not
establish KV corruption.

Could maintainers advise whether cross-mode consistency of these autotuned
RMSNorm launch configurations is expected, and where a regression test for
this initial-prefill behavior should live?

### 🐛 Describe the bug `Scheduler.reset_prefix_cache(reset_running_requests=True)` preempts every running request outside `schedule()`. It is called from `pause_generation(mode="keep")`, where `clear_cache=True` is the default, and from `sleep(level>=1, mode="keep")`. Because the preemption happens outside `schedule()`, the next `schedule()` re-admits those requests right away. The comment at `vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py:2789` says this is intended. The same `SchedulerOutput` then reports each request both as scheduled and in `preempted_req_ids`. `MooncakeStoreScheduler` handles this in the wrong order: 1. During `schedule()`, `update_state_after_alloc` rebuilds `_unfinished_requests[req_id]` (and `load_specs[req_id]` on a store hit). 2. `build_connector_meta` then processes `preempted_req_ids` and pops those entries (`mooncake/store/scheduler.py:226-231`). 3. The request is processed as scheduled, but its state is gone: - V2 model runner, request in `scheduled_new_reqs`: `assert request.req_id in self._unfinished_requests` fails at `scheduler.py:245` - V1 model runner, request in `resumed_req_ids` (any role except a pure `kv_consumer` without `save_decode_cache`): `TypeError: 'NoneType' object is not subscriptable` at `scheduler.py:298` - Async load (`load_async=True`, the default) after a reset without `reset_connector`, e.g. `LLM.reset_prefix_cache(True)`: the fresh load spec is dropped, no load is issued, and the request waits in `WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS` forever The first two raise inside `schedule()` and kill EngineCore. The `reset_store` docstring names RL weight-update workflows as the intended caller, so `pause_generation(mode="keep")` followed by `resume_generation()` is an expected path. **Minimal repro**: ```python import sys from types import SimpleNamespace sys.path.insert(0, "tests/v1/kv_connector/unit") from test_mooncake_store_scheduler import _make_bare_scheduler from tests.v1.core.utils import MockKVConfig, create_requests, create_scheduler from vllm.v1.core.sched.interface import PauseState from vllm.v1.outputs import ModelRunnerOutput sched = create_scheduler( enable_prefix_caching=True, use_kv_connector=MockKVConfig(matched_tokens=0, is_async=False), use_v2_model_runner=True, ) mooncake = _make_bare_scheduler() mooncake._unfinished_request_ids = set() mooncake.client = SimpleNamespace(discard=lambda *_: None) sched.connector.get_num_new_matched_tokens = lambda req, n: (0, False) sched.connector.update_state_after_alloc = mooncake.update_state_after_alloc sched.connector.build_connector_meta = mooncake.build_connector_meta reqs = create_requests(num_requests=2, num_tokens=40) for r in reqs: sched.add_request(r) out = sched.schedule() sched.update_from_output( out, ModelRunnerOutput( req_ids=[r.request_id for r in reqs], req_id_to_index={r.request_id: i for i, r in enumerate(reqs)}, sampled_token_ids=[[1] for _ in reqs], ), ) sched.set_pause_state(PauseState.PAUSED_ALL) sched.reset_prefix_cache(reset_running_requests=True) sched.set_pause_state(PauseState.UNPAUSED) sched.schedule() ``` Output: ```text File ".../kv_connector/v1/mooncake/store/scheduler.py", line 245, in build_connector_meta assert request.req_id in self._unfinished_requests AssertionError ``` With `use_v2_model_runner=False`: ```text File ".../kv_connector/v1/mooncake/store/scheduler.py", line 298, in build_connector_meta request_real = request_tuple[0] # type: ignore[index] TypeError: 'NoneType' object is not subscriptable ``` ### Before submitting a new issue... - items.title: [Bug]: validate_xgrammar_grammar skips unsupported-feature checks for JSON schemas nested in structural tags
items.body:
`validate_xgrammar_grammar()` does not check JSON schemas nested inside a structural tag for features xgrammar does not support, so those constraints are silently dropped.

For plain `json` constraints, `has_xgrammar_unsupported_json_features()` rejects schemas that xgrammar would compile incorrectly (e.g. `multipleOf`, which xgrammar ignores with only a log warning). With the default `backend="auto"`, that rejection is what triggers the fallback to guidance/outlines. The `structural_tag` branch only tries to compile the tag, so any `json_schema` inside it skips this check: validation passes, the request stays on xgrammar, and the output can violate the schema.

A schema ends up inside a structural tag in at least three ways, all reproduced below with `{"type": "number", "multipleOf": 0.5}`, where the compiled grammar accepts `0.3`:

1. A user-supplied `structural_tag` (`response_format` or `structured_outputs`), in both the new (`format`) and legacy (`structures`/`triggers`) shapes.
2. Parameter schemas of strict tools, for any `tool_choice` that builds a tool-call tag (`required`, `auto`, named).
3. Harmony (gpt-oss), which wraps every `response_format` / `structured_outputs` constraint into a structural tag, even without tools.

The same schema passed as plain `json` is rejected, as expected.

Reproduced on `main` at `2b9b55c7f1` with xgrammar 0.2.7.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction script and output</summary>

```python
import json
from unittest.mock import MagicMock

from xgrammar import Grammar
from xgrammar.testing import _is_grammar_accept_string

from vllm.entrypoints.generate.base.protocol import validate_structural_tag_payload
from vllm.entrypoints.openai.chat_completion.protocol import (
    ChatCompletionRequest,
    ChatCompletionToolsParam,
)
from vllm.parser.abstract_parser import DelegatingParser
from vllm.parser.harmony import _adjust_output_format
from vllm.sampling_params import SamplingParams, StructuredOutputsParams
from vllm.tool_parsers.qwen3_engine_tool_parser import Qwen3EngineToolParser
from vllm.v1.structured_output.backend_xgrammar import validate_xgrammar_grammar

schema = {
    "type": "object",
    "properties": {"value": {"type": "number", "multipleOf": 0.5}},
    "required": ["value"],
}


def validate(so: StructuredOutputsParams) -> str:
    try:
        validate_xgrammar_grammar(SamplingParams(structured_outputs=so))
        return "PASSED"
    except Exception as e:
        return f"RAISED {type(e).__name__}: {e}"


def accepts(tag: str, template: str) -> str:
    g = Grammar.from_structural_tag(tag)
    return ", ".join(
        f"{v}={_is_grammar_accept_string(g, template.format(v))}"
        for v in ("0.5", "0.3")
    )


print("-- baseline: plain json")
print(f"   validation {validate(StructuredOutputsParams(json=schema))}")

print("-- 1. user structural_tag")
new_style = {
    "type": "structural_tag",
    "format": {
        "type": "sequence",
        "elements": [
            {"type": "const_string", "value": "Answer: "},
            {"type": "json_schema", "json_schema": schema},
        ],
    },
}
legacy = {
    "type": "structural_tag",
    "structures": [{"begin": "Answer: ", "schema": schema, "end": ""}],
    "triggers": ["Answer: "],
}
for name, tag in (("new-style", new_style), ("legacy", legacy)):
    s = json.dumps(tag)
    validate_structural_tag_payload(s, parameter="response_format")
    print(f"   {name}: validation "
          f"{validate(StructuredOutputsParams(structural_tag=s))}")
    if name == "new-style":
        print(f"   {name}: accepts {accepts(s, 'Answer: {{\"value\": {}}}')}")

print("-- 2. strict tool parameter schema")
tools = [
    ChatCompletionToolsParam(
        type="function",
        function={"name": "set_temp", "parameters": schema, "strict": True},
    )
]


class QwenParser(DelegatingParser):
    tool_parser_cls = Qwen3EngineToolParser


call = (
    "<tool_call>\n<function=set_temp>\n<parameter=value>\n{}\n"
    "</parameter>\n</function>\n</tool_call>"
)
for tool_choice in ("required", "auto"):
    req = ChatCompletionRequest(
        messages=[], model="m", tools=tools, tool_choice=tool_choice
    )
    so = QwenParser(MagicMock(), tools=tools).adjust_request(req).structured_outputs
    print(f"   tool_choice={tool_choice}: validation {validate(so)}")
    print(f"   tool_choice={tool_choice}: accepts {accepts(so.structural_tag, call)}")

print("-- 3. Harmony (gpt-oss) response_format, no tools")
req = ChatCompletionRequest(
    messages=[], model="m", structured_outputs=StructuredOutputsParams(json=schema)
)
so = _adjust_output_format(req).structured_outputs
final = '<|channel|>final <|constrain|>json<|message|>{{"value": {}}}<|end|>'
print(f"   validation {validate(so)}")
print(f"   accepts {accepts(so.structural_tag, final)}")
```

Output (xgrammar's own `multipleOf is not supported ... ignoring` warnings omitted):

```text
-- baseline: plain json
   validation RAISED VLLMValidationError: The provided JSON schema contains features not supported by xgrammar.
-- 1. user structural_tag
   new-style: validation PASSED
   new-style: accepts 0.5=True, 0.3=True
   legacy: validation PASSED
-- 2. strict tool parameter schema
   tool_choice=required: validation PASSED
   tool_choice=required: accepts 0.5=True, 0.3=True
   tool_choice=auto: validation PASSED
   tool_choice=auto: accepts 0.5=True, 0.3=True
-- 3. Harmony (gpt-oss) response_format, no tools
   validation PASSED
   accepts 0.5=True, 0.3=True
```

</details>

items.title: [ROCm] AITER v0.1.23 bump: gfx950 a16w4 MXFP4 MoE Gluon backend crashes (AttributeError get_scaled_upcast_fp4_scale_layout)
items.body:
## Report of bug

Bumping AITER to v0.1.23 (#58867) surfaced two upstream regressions, one already fixed in that PR and one filed upstream for tracking.

### 1. `upcast_from_mxfp` removed from `aiter.ops.triton.moe.quant_moe` (fixed)

ROCm/aiter#5259 removed the public `upcast_from_mxfp` helper with no replacement shipped in the pip package. Only used by `tests/kernels/moe/test_ocp_mx_moe.py`, which had its own equivalent pure-PyTorch `mxfp4_dequantize` helper already — fixed by reusing that instead of the aiter import (already included in #58867).

### 2. gfx950 `moe_gemm_a16w4` Gluon backend crash (production-path regression)

ROCm/aiter#5355 (in v0.1.23) added a Gluon-based `moe_gemm_a16w4` kernel for gfx950 and widened `_GLUON_SUPPORTED_ARCHS` to include it, so the default (`backend=None`) auto-detect on gfx950 now always routes to Gluon. That kernel calls `gl.amd.get_scaled_upcast_fp4_scale_layout(...)`, a Triton-Gluon AMD API only added upstream in triton-lang/triton#11470 (merged 2026-09-08) — newer than the Triton commit vLLM's ROCm images currently pin (`669b31a`, 2026-08-28) — causing:

```
AttributeError("module 'triton.experimental.gluon.language.amd' has no attribute 'get_scaled_upcast_fp4_scale_layout'")
```

This hits `vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/experts/aiter_mxfp4_w4a16_moe.py`, i.e. any gfx950 (MI355) model using AITER's a16w4 MXFP4 MoE path (e.g. gpt-oss), not just tests.

Filed upstream: ROCm/aiter#5888.

**Workaround applied in #58867**: pass `backend="triton"` explicitly on gfx950 for both `moe_gemm_a16w4()` calls, forcing the known-good path until aiter guards its Gluon auto-detect against this Triton version gap (or vLLM's pinned Triton is updated past triton-lang/triton#11470).

### Confirmation

Filing this mainly for tracking/visibility — the fix is already in #58867. Will close once that PR merges, or if the aiter-side fix (ROCm/aiter#5888) lands and we want to revert the workaround.

### Before submitting a new issue

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the vLLM community for help

items.title: [Bug]: Intermittent Xid 31 MMU fault in pynccl all_reduce during CUDA graph
items.body:
### Your current environment

vLLM 0.29.0 (image vllm/vllm-openai:v0.29.0 + ray 2.56.1, pip package b12x 1.3.0)
torch 2.13.0+cu130, CUDA 13.0, transformers 5.16.1
GPU: 6x NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition (SM120), driver 595.91.07
Host: Ubuntu, kernel 7.0.0-31-generic, Docker
Cluster: two nodes (4 + 2 GPUs), Ray 2.56.1, 100 GbE direct link
Model: nvidia/GLM-5.2-NVFP4, PP=3 / TP=2, VLLM_PP_LAYER_PARTITION=31,29,18

Launch command:

  vllm serve nvidia/GLM-5.2-NVFP4 --distributed-executor-backend ray \
    --pipeline-parallel-size 3 --tensor-parallel-size 2 \
    --kernel-config '{"moe_backend":"b12x","linear_backend":"flashinfer_b12x",
                      "enable_cutedsl_warmup":true,"enable_flashinfer_autotune":true}' \
    --attention-config '{"sparse_mla_force_mqa":true}' \
    --disable-custom-all-reduce --no-async-scheduling \
    --max-model-len 262144 --max-num-batched-tokens 2048 --max-num-seqs 32 \
    --gpu-memory-utilization 0.98

Note: --disable-custom-all-reduce is required on SM120, so every reduction goes
through the pynccl path.

(collect_env.py output can be provided on request - the engine runs inside a
container on a two-node Ray cluster, so the script does not capture the full
picture.)


### 🐛 Describe the bug

Roughly every third engine start dies during CUDA graph capture. The crash is a
driver-level Xid 31 MMU fault; on the Python side it surfaces as an NCCL error
inside the tensor-parallel all_reduce that is being captured. It is intermittent:
the identical command succeeds on the next attempt, and once the engine is up it
serves for days without a single Xid.

Kernel log:

    NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:41:00): 31, pid=147307, name=ray::vllm_Worke,
    channel 0x00000002, intr 00000000. MMU Fault: ENGINE GRAPHICS GPC0
    GPCCLIENT_T1_0 faulted @ 0x284_e8006000.
    Fault is of type FAULT_PDE ACCESS_TYPE_VIRT_READ

Engine log - the crash happens at "Capturing CUDA graphs (FULL): 71%|5/7",
in Worker_PP1_TP0:

    reduced = tensor_model_parallel_all_reduce(hidden_states)
      -> get_tp_group().all_reduce(input_)
      -> torch.ops.vllm.all_reduce(input_, group_name=...)
      -> group._all_reduce_out_place(tensor)
      -> self.device_communicator.all_reduce(input_)
      -> out = pynccl_comm.all_reduce(input_)
      -> self.nccl.ncclAllReduce(...)
      -> RuntimeError: NCCL error: unhandled cuda error
    During handling of the above exception, another exception occurred:
      torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered

## Controlled comparison

Same hardware, same command, only --enforce-eager added. All other models shut
down, GPUs verified free between runs:

    with graph capture   first-attempt failures ~30 % (6 of 22)   startup ~3:00 min
    --enforce-eager      first-attempt failures 0 of 8            startup ~1:45 min

22 first attempts recorded over five days; 6 died this way. Two further failures
were an unrelated out-of-memory condition and are excluded. In a deliberate
reproduction run today the failure appeared on the 4th consecutive start.

Seven Xid occurrences so far, on all four GPUs of the head node (PCI 01:00,
21:00, 41:00, 61:00), so this is not a defective card. The faulting addresses
repeat across incidents (0x284_e8006000 four times, 0x24f_78006000 twice).

## What we ruled out

- GPU memory pressure: same behaviour at --gpu-memory-utilization 0.97 and 0.98.
  At crash time the cards sit at 95.8 GiB of 97.9 GiB, 350 W power cap, 33 C.
- Defective hardware: all four GPUs of the head node produced the fault.
- #50189: that is a *write* fault under concurrent load with the flashinfer_b12x
  MoE backend. We use the native b12x MoE backend, our fault is a *read* at
  startup, and the engine never faults while serving.
- #40742: requires PDL (we set neither TRTLLM_ENABLE_PDL nor
  TORCHINDUCTOR_ENABLE_PDL) and raises "operation not permitted when stream is
  capturing", not a driver Xid.
- #30044: GH200, no Xid, deterministic rather than intermittent.

## Guess at the mechanism

Capturing an ncclAllReduce inside a CUDA graph appears to hit a race. The
faulting addresses repeat across incidents, which looks more like a deterministic
allocation being touched at the wrong moment than random corruption. We cannot
verify this from the outside.

## Workaround

Our autostart script retries up to five times, waiting for all GPUs to be
released between attempts; attempt 1 or 2 normally succeeds. --enforce-eager
avoids the fault entirely at the cost of throughput.

Full engine log, dmesg excerpt and nvidia-smi output of a failing run are saved
and can be attached on request.



### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

items.title: [Bug]: DeepSeek-V4-Flash + DFlash speculator fails at startup (fp8_ds_mla draft KV dtype; 16384 vs 4096 hidden states)
items.body:
### Your current environment

vLLM `main` @ 73a78e6f1f, 2× B300 (SM100), TP2 + expert parallel. Reproduced with `--load-format dummy` (the failures are at startup, before any weights matter).

### 🐛 Describe the bug

`DeepSeek-V4-Flash` + the `RedHatAI/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-speculator.dflash` DFlash drafter fails at startup on current `main`, in one of two ways depending on the drafter's KV cache dtype.

**1. fp8 target KV cache (default draft KV dtype): no attention backend for the drafter**

```bash
vllm serve RedHatAI/DeepSeek-V4-Flash --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 --trust-remote-code \
  --max-model-len 131072 --tensor-parallel-size 2 --enable-expert-parallel \
  --block-size 256 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --load-format dummy --enforce-eager \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dflash","model":"RedHatAI/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-speculator.dflash","num_speculative_tokens":7}'
```

The drafter's sliding-window layers inherit the target's `fp8_ds_mla` KV cache dtype, which no non-MLA backend supports:

```
ValueError: No valid attention backend found for cuda with AttentionSelectorConfig(head_size=256, dtype=torch.bfloat16, kv_cache_dtype=fp8_ds_mla, block_size=256, use_mla=False, ..., has_sliding_window=True, ...). Reasons: {FLASHINFER: [kv_cache_dtype not supported], FLASH_ATTN: [kv_cache_dtype not supported, FP8 KV cache requires FA3 on SM90, FA4 with head_size=512 on SM90, or FA4 on SM100], TRITON_ATTN: [kv_cache_dtype not supported], FLEX_ATTENTION: [kv_cache_dtype not supported], TURBOQUANT: [kv_cache_dtype not supported, sliding window not supported]}.
```

(Forcing `"attention_backend": "FLASH_ATTN"` in the speculative config fails the same way: `kv_cache_dtype not supported`.)

**2. bf16 draft KV cache: hidden-state width mismatch in `propose`**

Same command, with `"attention_backend":"FLASH_ATTN","kv_cache_dtype":"auto"` added to the speculative config. The backend check passes, and the profile run then fails:

```
File "vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py", line 947, in profile_run
File "vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py", line 887, in _dummy_run
File "vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/dflash/speculator.py", line 376, in propose
    self.hidden_states[:num_target_tokens].copy_(hidden_states[:num_target_tokens])
RuntimeError: The size of tensor a (16384) must match the size of tensor b (4096) at non-singleton dimension 1
```

`aux_hidden_states` is empty here, so `propose` falls back to the target's final hidden states. For DeepSeek-V4 those are 16384 wide (4 hyper-connection streams × 4096), while the drafter's buffer is 4096 wide. It looks like DeepSeek-V4 doesn't expose aux hidden states for DFlash, similar to what #55682 adds for GLM-5.3-Flash.

**Expected:** DeepSeek-V4-Flash + its DFlash speculator starts. Suggested fixes: pick a draft KV cache dtype the draft's backend supports instead of inheriting `fp8_ds_mla`, and capture the aux hidden states DFlash expects from DeepSeek-V4.

For reference, `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-DSpark` (bundled DSpark drafter) starts fine on the same setup.

Found while testing KV cache grouping for #58638. AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to reproduce and write this up; I reviewed it.

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

items.title: [Bug]: When using the V4 parser in vLLM to parse outputs from DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, the leading extra space in V4.1 DSML tags breaks state machine matching and parameter regex, filters arg deltas, and prevents streaming return of tool call arguments.
items.body:
### Your current environment
The output of python collect_env.py ```text Your output of `python collect_env.py` here ```
### 🐛 Describe the bug vLLM does not ship a dedicated parser for DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, and reuses the existing V4 parser to process model outputs generated by V4.1 Flash. DeepSeek V4.1 Flash introduces an extra leading space inside DSML tags compared to the V4 specification. This difference triggers multiple failures in the legacy V4 parser: 1. The state machine for DSML tag matching fails to recognize tags due to the unexpected leading space. 2. The hardcoded regular expressions used in `_dsml_arg_converter` cannot match the parameter content, as the regex patterns do not account for the leading space. 3. The argument delta filtering logic with `arg_structural_chars=frozenset(">")` buffers all delta content that does not contain the `>` character and suppresses incremental streaming delivery. As a combined result, tool call arguments cannot be streamed back to the caller. The proposed fix is to implement a new V4.1-specific parser inheriting from the V4 parser class: adjust tag definitions and regular expressions to accommodate the leading space, disable the arg delta filtering logic, and register the parser under an independent name. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

items.title: [Bug][ROCm]: v0.30.0 release is missing #57252, so GLM-5.3 (GlmMoeDsa) can't start on AMD
items.body:
### Your current environment

<details>
<summary>collect_env highlights (full output available)</summary>

```
vLLM Version                 : 0.30.0
PyTorch version              : 2.12.0+git6bbd260
ROCM Version                 : 7.2.53211-c2d9476115
HIP runtime version          : 7.2.53211
amd-aiter                    : 0.1.21.post2
transformers                 : 5.17.0
GPU                          : 8x AMD Instinct MI325X (gfx942), driver 6.19.14.31400100
```

</details>

Image `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:v0.30.0` as published, with no custom layers and no entrypoint override (the pod reports `docker.io/vllm/vllm-openai-rocm@sha256:2e7da1ad1c66836802072588adea75f9f4991da5f9545b4318e91d422c22ce6a`). Model `zai-org/GLM-5.3` at revision `aca966e4e02791568aa6a4ced368624b3d897f42`, native FP8, which resolves to `GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM` with `DeepseekV32MTPModel` as the drafter. One Kubernetes node, TP 8.

```
vllm serve zai-org/GLM-5.3 --port 8000 --tensor-parallel-size 8 --max-model-len 262144 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 --revision aca966e4e02791568aa6a4ced368624b3d897f42 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --speculative-config.method mtp --speculative-config.num_speculative_tokens 5 \
  --tool-call-parser glm47 --enable-auto-tool-choice --reasoning-parser glm45 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 --max-num-seqs 128 --safetensors-load-strategy prefetch \
  --enable-prefix-caching --linear-backend aiter --moe-backend aiter
```

Env: `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`, `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=1`, `VLLM_EXECUTE_MODEL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=1800`, `PYTHONHASHSEED=0`. These are the AMD flags from the GLM-5.3 recipe plus our sizing, and the same block runs on v0.29.0.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

The engine dies in `profile_run` about two minutes into init, on every start, and the pod crash-loops. We first hit it on our own build (the official image plus a tokenizer package), then reproduced it on the plain official image above on 2026-09-23. Every TP worker raises the same error while `torch.compile` traces the model:

```
File ".../vllm/v1/worker/gpu_worker.py", line 572, in determine_available_memory
  self.model_runner.profile_run()
File ".../vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py", line 6524, in profile_run
File ".../vllm/model_executor/models/deepseek_v2.py", line 1968, in forward
File ".../vllm/model_executor/layers/mla.py", line 235, in forward
  self.mla_attn.impl.record_logical_topk_ready()
torch._dynamo.exc.ObservedAttributeError: ConstantVariable(str: "'ROCMAiterMLASparseImpl' object has no attribute 'record_logical_topk_ready'")
```

It's the regression from #57248, which was reported for GLM-5.3-Flash on a nightly and fixed on main by #57252. The fix didn't make it into v0.30.0: the tag's `rocm_aiter_mla_sparse.py` has no such method, and `releases/v0.30.0` last moved on 2026-09-21 without it. The `v0.30.1rc0` tag has the fix, but it's on main, so as far as we can tell nothing ships it before 0.31.0.

It isn't limited to Flash. The call at `mla.py:235` runs on every sparse MLA layer, and on ROCm the only sparse backend is `ROCM_AITER_MLA_SPARSE`, so no flag avoids it. #56604 notes the same crash on `GLM-5.2-FP8`, and the same call sits in `models/deepseek_v32/attention.py:496`, so DeepSeek-V3.2 on ROCm should fail too (we haven't run it). The GLM-5.3 and DeepSeek-V3.2 recipes both send AMD users to `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:latest`, which is v0.30.0 today.

Could #57252 go into a v0.30.1? If a patch release isn't planned, a known-issues line on the v0.30.0 release would save the next AMD user some time.

### Workaround

Adding the #57252 method to the installed file before `vllm serve` starts gets it running:

```python
def record_logical_topk_ready(self) -> None:
    pass
```

With that one change, the block starts in about 6.5 minutes, passes a known-answer prompt, a tool call and a 4 of 4 needle recall at 50K tokens, and served a 3 hour agentic load test through our gateway (8,272 requests, 0 errors).

items.title: [Bug]: Triton fused MoE incorrectly indexes per-channel weight scales with per-tensor activations
items.body:
### Your current environment

Component validation environment:
- GPU: NVIDIA L20
- PyTorch: 2.13.0+cu129
- CUDA reported by PyTorch: 12.9
- Input dtype: BF16 for the scale-indexing reproducer

The component experiments used an overlay of relevant vLLM Python sources
with an existing compiled runtime, rather than a complete build at one
revision. The affected code was subsequently checked at
`00b7847c8036b667742b4efb21aab1de51fd4721`;

### 🐛 Describe the bug

`QuarkW8A8Int8MoEMethod` supports static per-tensor activation scales
together with per-output-channel weight scales. However, the legacy
Triton MoE path uses the activation quantization flag to select both
activation-scale and weight-scale indexing.

For this combination, `per_act_token_quant=False`, so the kernel takes
the tensor-scale branch even though the weights have per-channel scales.
It consequently reads the weight scales using the wrong layout.

This affects the existing static INT8 path independently of its planned
migration to the MoE oracle.

### Expected behavior

Activation and weight scales should be indexed independently:

- A1/A2: use the loaded static scalar activation scales.
- W13/W2: use the scale belonging to the routed expert and output channel.

Changing relevant weight scales should affect the corresponding
computation, while changing scales belonging only to unrouted experts
should not affect the output.

### Observed behavior and reproduction outline

A component probe used:
- 4 experts
- Hidden size and intermediate size of 128
- 8 tokens, top-k=2
- BF16 inputs
- Static activation scales and nonuniform per-channel weight scales
- No bias, with router weights applied on the output side

The probe exercised Quark weight creation and post-load processing,
then its existing `apply()` path.

With fixed weights, inputs, and routing, multiplying all W13 channel
scales of expert 3 by 4 produced no output change, although that expert
was selected by four routing slots.

An experimental patch separating weight-scale layout from activation
quantization made this perturbation affect the output. The corrected
legacy and manually constructed modular paths also produced identical
BF16 outputs for the covered case.

These are component-level observations, not a completed model evaluation
or full regression result. The modular comparison bypassed backend
selection and does not establish static INT8 oracle support.

### Suspected root cause

There are two related problems:

1. `int8_w8a8_moe_quant_config()` currently sets
   `per_out_ch_quant=False`.
2. The legacy wrapper and `TritonExperts` pass
   `per_act_token_quant` as the GEMM kernel's `per_channel_quant` flag.

In the shared non-block W8A8 kernel, that flag selects both per-token
activation-scale reads and per-channel weight-scale reads. The tensor
branch instead loads one activation scale and indexes the weight scale
as one scalar per expert.

Relevant code at the inspected revision:
- [INT8 quant-config factory](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/00b7847c8036b667742b4efb21aab1de51fd4721/vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/config.py#L628)
- [Shared scale indexing](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/00b7847c8036b667742b4efb21aab1de51fd4721/vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/fused_moe.py#L483)
- [Legacy config forwarding](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/00b7847c8036b667742b4efb21aab1de51fd4721/vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/fused_moe.py#L1619)

### Proposed fix

I propose separating activation-scale and weight-scale indexing in the
shared INT8/FP8 non-block Triton path, using the independent granularity
information already represented by `FusedMoEQuantConfig`.

This would include propagating both flags through the call chain and
correcting callers that currently rely on the coupled behavior without
explicitly declaring their actual weight-scale layout.

The scope would remain scale layout and indexing. Block quantization,
quantization algorithms, backend selection, compute dtype, and
router-weight ordering would retain their existing behavior.

FP8 is part of the compatibility and regression scope because it shares
this implementation; I am not reporting a separately reproduced FP8
failure here.

### Related issue

Related to #57092, which fixes per-token activations with per-tensor
weight scales. This report concerns the opposite combination:
per-tensor activations with per-channel weight scales, reproduced
through Quark static INT8.

That combination remains skipped in #57092's updated combination tests.
The proposed fix would preserve its stride/broadcast corrections while
separating activation-scale and weight-scale indexing.

This is also a correctness prerequisite for the Quark static INT8
oracle migration tracked in #54959.

I would like to submit this correctness fix separately, followed by the
static INT8 oracle migration. 

<details>
<summary>Supplementary component reproducer (not yet GPU-validated)</summary>

This is a deterministic version of the component probe, with separate W13/W2 channel-scale checks and an unrouted-expert control. Its syntax and expected values have been checked locally, but **this exact script has not yet been run on a GPU**. The earlier observations above came from the original overlay probes.

Save as `repro_quark_static_int8_scales.py` in a working CUDA vLLM checkout. Run with its configured environment and an available GPU (replace `4` as appropriate):

```bash
git rev-parse HEAD
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=4 .venv/bin/python repro_quark_static_int8_scales.py > repro-58532.log 2>&1
```

The script uses synthetic weights and requires no model download. Expected outputs are explained in its docstring. Numerical failures return exit code 1; runtime errors are not swallowed. Source inspection predicts that the routed W13/W2 perturbation checks fail on the affected implementation; this is not a new measured result.

```python
"""Deterministic component reproducer for vllm-project/vllm#58532.

Run with a working CUDA vLLM installation; no checkpoint is downloaded.
This uses Quark's static legacy path, including create/post-load/apply.
It does not patch vLLM, bypass selector checks to construct a modular kernel,
or validate a full model. Nonzero exit means a failed assertion or runtime error.

The weights are INT8 identity matrices (gate, up, and down). With x=1,
A1=A2=1/16 and weight scales=1, each expert returns 12/16 = 0.75:
  GEMM1 -> gate=up=1; SiLU(1)*1 -> BF16 -> INT8 value 12.
Top-k=2 with weights 0.5 preserves 0.75 after reduction.

Doubling only expert 3's gate channel 0 scale gives gate=2, up=1;
SiLU(2)*1 -> BF16 -> INT8 value 28, hence expert output 28/16=1.75.
Rows routed to expert 3 therefore have output[0] = (1.75+0.75)/2 = 1.25.
Doubling its down-projection channel 0 scale instead gives 1.125 there.
All these final values are exactly representable in BF16. The tested values
are away from INT8 rounding ties and saturation, so exact checks are intended.

This newly prepared script has not yet been GPU-validated. It replaces the
earlier random sensitivity probe with a hand-checkable construction.
"""

import json
import subprocess
from pathlib import Path

import torch

import vllm
from vllm.config import VllmConfig, set_current_vllm_config
from vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe.activation import MoEActivation
from vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe.config import (
    FusedMoEConfig,
    FusedMoEParallelConfig,
    RoutingMethodType,
)
from vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.quark.quark_moe import (
    QuarkW8A8Int8MoEMethod,
)
from vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils.quant_utils import (
    kInt8StaticChannelSym,
    kInt8StaticTensorSym,
)
from vllm.v1.worker.workspace import init_workspace_manager


def emit(**values):
    print(json.dumps(values), flush=True)


@torch.inference_mode()
def run():
    device = torch.device("cuda:0")
    dtype = torch.bfloat16
    experts, hidden, intermediate, tokens, topk = 4, 128, 128, 8, 2
    init_workspace_manager(device)
    config = FusedMoEConfig(
        num_experts=experts,
        num_local_experts=experts,
        num_logical_experts=experts,
        experts_per_token=topk,
        hidden_dim=hidden,
        intermediate_size=intermediate,
        activation=MoEActivation.SILU,
        device="cuda",
        routing_method=RoutingMethodType.Default,
        moe_parallel_config=FusedMoEParallelConfig.make_no_parallel(),
        in_dtype=dtype,
        has_bias=False,
        moe_backend="triton",
        max_num_tokens=tokens,
    )
    method = QuarkW8A8Int8MoEMethod(
        config, kInt8StaticChannelSym, kInt8StaticTensorSym
    )
    layer = torch.nn.Module()
    layer.intermediate_size_per_partition = intermediate
    layer.local_num_experts = experts
    layer.global_num_experts = experts
    layer.activation = MoEActivation.SILU
    layer.expert_map = None
    layer.apply_router_weight_on_input = False
    with torch.device(device):
        method.create_weights(layer, experts, hidden, intermediate, dtype)

    eye = torch.eye(hidden, dtype=torch.float32, device=device).to(torch.int8)
    layer.w13_weight.copy_(torch.cat((eye, eye), dim=0).unsqueeze(0))
    layer.w2_weight.copy_(eye.unsqueeze(0))
    layer.w13_weight_scale.fill_(1.0)
    layer.w2_weight_scale.fill_(1.0)
    layer.w13_input_scale.fill_(1.0 / 16)
    layer.w2_input_scale.fill_(1.0 / 16)
    method.process_weights_after_loading(layer)
    if method.moe_kernel is not None:
        raise RuntimeError("This reproducer targets the static legacy path before PR B")

    x = torch.ones((tokens, hidden), dtype=dtype, device=device)
    # Expert 3 receives four slots; expert 2 receives none.
    ids = torch.tensor([[3, 1], [0, 1]] * 4, dtype=torch.int32, device=device)
    weights = torch.full((tokens, topk), 0.5, device=device)
    routed_to_3 = (ids == 3).any(dim=1)
    expected_base = torch.full_like(x, 0.75)
    failures = []

    def forward():
        result = method.apply(layer, x.clone(), weights, ids, None, None)
        torch.cuda.synchronize()
        return result.clone()

    def check(name, actual, expected):
        emit(
            case=name,
            actual_channel_0=actual[:, 0].float().tolist(),
            expected_channel_0=expected[:, 0].float().tolist(),
            max_abs_error=(actual.float() - expected.float()).abs().max().item(),
        )
        try:
            torch.testing.assert_close(actual, expected, rtol=0, atol=0)
        except AssertionError as error:
            failures.append(name)
            print(f"FAIL {name}: {error}", flush=True)
        else:
            print(f"PASS {name}", flush=True)

    baseline = forward()
    check("baseline", baseline, expected_base)
    check("repeatability", forward(), baseline)
    for attr, expected_value in (
        ("w13_weight_scale", 1.25),
        ("w2_weight_scale", 1.125),
    ):
        scale = getattr(layer, attr)
        saved = scale.clone()
        try:
            scale[3, 0].mul_(2)
            expected = expected_base.clone()
            expected[routed_to_3, 0] = expected_value
            check(f"{attr}: routed expert 3, channel 0 x2", forward(), expected)
        finally:
            scale.copy_(saved)
        try:
            scale[2].mul_(4)
            check(f"{attr}: unrouted expert 2 x4", forward(), expected_base)
        finally:
            scale.copy_(saved)

    if failures:
        emit(result="FAIL", failed_cases=failures)
        raise SystemExit(1)
    emit(result="PASS")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    if not torch.cuda.is_available():
        raise RuntimeError("A CUDA GPU and a working CUDA vLLM installation are required")
    source_dir = Path(vllm.__file__).resolve().parent
    revision = subprocess.run(
        ["git", "-C", str(source_dir), "rev-parse", "HEAD"],
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
        check=False,
    )
    emit(
        torch=torch.__version__,
        cuda=torch.version.cuda,
        vllm_version=vllm.__version__,
        vllm_file=str(vllm.__file__),
        source_git_head=revision.stdout.strip() if revision.returncode == 0 else None,
        gpu=torch.cuda.get_device_name(0),
    )
    with set_current_vllm_config(VllmConfig()):
        run()
```

</details>

items.title: [Bug]: Responses API `truncation: "auto"` truncates at the token level from the left, dropping `instructions` first and cutting mid-item
items.body:
### Your current environment

vLLM `main` (also affects the pending Harmony fixes #38143 / #39413). The field exists but was a no-op in v0.15.1.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

`truncation: "auto"` on `/v1/responses` is implemented by mapping the request to
`truncate_prompt_tokens=-1`:

- `vllm/entrypoints/openai/responses/serving.py` (main), inside `get_max_tokens(...)`:
  `truncate_prompt_tokens=(-1 if request.truncation != "disabled" else None)` — appears twice (initial request and the built-in-tools loop).
- `-1` resolves to `max_model_len` in `vllm/entrypoints/utils.py::_validate_truncation_size`, and the prompt is then cut to the **last** N tokens of the fully rendered prompt (`SamplingParams.truncate_prompt_tokens` docstring: "will use only the last k tokens from the prompt (i.e., left truncation)").

That differs from the OpenAI spec this field is meant to mirror (`openai-python`, `response_create_params.py`):

> `auto`: If the input to this Response exceeds the model's context window size, the model will truncate the response to fit the context window by **dropping items from the beginning of the conversation**.

Two consequences of the current implementation:

1. **`instructions` is discarded first.** `instructions` is a top-level parameter, not an input item, so under the spec it is never dropped. In vLLM it is rendered as the system/developer message at the head of the token sequence, so it is the first thing a left cut removes. The model then answers with no instructions while the response object still reports `truncation: "auto"`.
2. **Truncation is not item-aligned.** The cut can land in the middle of a message, or in the middle of the chat-template header, leaving the model a prompt that starts with half a message and stray template tokens.

### Expected behavior

Match the spec: drop whole items from the front of `input` until the rendered prompt fits `max_model_len - max_output_tokens`, keep `instructions` (and the final user item) intact, and never split an item. If a single item is itself too large to fit, return the existing 400 rather than silently truncating inside it.

### Suggested fix

Implement `auto` at the item level in the Responses serving path before rendering (iteratively drop `input[0]`, re-render, re-count), and stop passing `truncate_prompt_tokens=-1` for this mode. #38143 / #39413 could adopt the same helper for the Harmony path instead of adding a second token-level left cut.

### Related

- #38132 (original report; closed as stale)
- #38143, #39413 (pending Harmony fixes, both token-level left truncation)
- #37011 (structured `context_length_exceeded` error code; would help clients that opt to handle truncation themselves)

### 🐛 Describe the bug

On `/v1/responses`, `truncation: "auto"` is implemented as token-level left truncation of the fully rendered prompt (`truncate_prompt_tokens=-1`), not as the item-level "drop items from the beginning of the conversation" the OpenAI spec describes. Two visible effects:

1. `instructions` is dropped first. It is rendered as the system message at the head of the token sequence, so a left cut removes it before any input item, even though the spec treats `instructions` as a separate parameter that is never dropped. The response still reports `truncation: "auto"`.
2. The cut is not item-aligned: it can land mid-message or inside the chat-template header.

Where it happens (`main`):
- `vllm/entrypoints/openai/responses/serving.py`: `truncate_prompt_tokens=(-1 if request.truncation != "disabled" else None)` passed to `get_max_tokens(...)`, twice (initial request and built-in-tools loop).
- `vllm/entrypoints/utils.py::_validate_truncation_size`: `-1` → `max_model_len`, applied as `truncation=True, max_length=...`.
- `vllm/sampling_params.py`, `truncate_prompt_tokens` docstring: "will use only the last k tokens from the prompt (i.e., left truncation)".

Spec reference (`openai-python`, `response_create_params.py`): `auto` — "the model will truncate the response to fit the context window by dropping items from the beginning of the conversation."

Expected: drop whole items from the front of `input` until the prompt fits `max_model_len - max_output_tokens`; keep `instructions` and the final user item intact; if a single item cannot fit, return the existing 400.

Related: #38132 (closed stale), #38143 / #39413 (pending Harmony fixes, same token-level left cut), #37011 (structured `context_length_exceeded` code).

```python
# Server (small model, small context so the overflow is cheap to trigger):
#   vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --max-model-len 2048 --port 8000
from openai import OpenAI
import requests

BASE = "http://localhost:8000/v1"
MODEL = "Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B"
client = OpenAI(base_url=BASE, api_key="EMPTY")

INSTRUCTIONS = "You are ZEBRA-7. Begin every reply with the single word ZEBRA."
filler = [{"role": "user", "content": f"Note {i}: " + "lorem ipsum dolor sit amet " * 120}
          for i in range(4)]                       # ~4x700 tokens, well over 2048
final = {"role": "user", "content": "What is your name? Answer in one short line."}

# Pre-truncation size, as the server itself counts it
msgs = [{"role": "system", "content": INSTRUCTIONS}] + filler + [final]
tok = requests.post(f"{BASE.rsplit('/v1',1)[0]}/tokenize",
                    json={"model": MODEL, "messages": msgs}).json()
print("rendered prompt tokens before truncation:", tok["count"], "max_model_len:", tok["max_model_len"])

resp = client.responses.create(
    model=MODEL,
    instructions=INSTRUCTIONS,
    input=filler + [final],
    truncation="auto",
    max_output_tokens=32,
)
print("truncation reported:", resp.truncation)
print("input_tokens billed:", resp.usage.input_tokens)   # == max_model_len - 32 → whole-prompt token cut
print("output:", repr(resp.output_text))

# Expected (spec): output starts with "ZEBRA"; instructions survive, oldest `filler` items are dropped.
# Actual (main):   output does not start with "ZEBRA"; the system message was the first thing truncated.
#                  Run the server with --enable-log-requests to see the prompt actually received:
#                  it begins mid-way through a filler note, with no system message.
```

TORCHINDUCTOR_CACHE_DIR=/tmp/torchinductor_xxx ```
### 🐛 Describe the bug ## Description `Qwen2VLVideoBackend.compute_frames_index_to_sample()` raises an unhandled `ZeroDivisionError` when a video contains exactly one decoded frame. Through the OpenAI-compatible API, this becomes an HTTP 500 response. The sampler rounds the available frame count down to a multiple of the default `temporal_patch_size=2`. For a one-frame video, that calculation produces `n=0`, but the function then uses `n` as a divisor. This report is specifically about the unhandled division by zero. Regardless of whether a one-frame video should be padded or rejected, it should not reach an internal arithmetic error. ## Reproduction Start vLLM: ```bash vllm serve Qwen/Qwen2-VL-2B-Instruct \ --served-model-name Qwen/Qwen2-VL-2B-Instruct \ --max-model-len 2048 \ --enforce-eager ``` Run the self-contained reproducer with [repro.py](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32563254/repro_qwen2vl.py): ```bash python repro.py ``` Observed output: ```text {"case": "one_frame", "status": 500, "body": "{\"error\":{\"message\":\"division by zero\"...}}"} {"case": "two_frame_control", "status": 200, ...} ``` `repro.py` sends two otherwise identical requests using embedded H.264 MP4 fixtures. The one-frame input fails, while the two-frame control succeeds. The server traceback ends at the frame-index calculation: ```text ZeroDivisionError: division by zero ``` Full log is here: [server_qwen2vl.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32563277/server_qwen2vl.log) ## Expected behavior The sampler should either: - produce a valid nonzero frame count, for example by repeating the single frame to satisfy the temporal patch size; or - reject the input with a clear validation error. It should not return HTTP 500 because of an unhandled `ZeroDivisionError`. ## Root cause For the failing input: ```text total_frames_num = 1 temporal_patch_size = 2 ``` `compute_frames_index_to_sample()` first rounds `max_frames` down to a multiple of `temporal_patch_size`: ```python max_frames = ( floor(min(max_frames, total_frames_num) / temporal_patch_size) * temporal_patch_size ) ``` This makes `max_frames` zero. The subsequent clamp and alignment also produce `n=0`. The function does not validate that result before evaluating: ```python torch.arange(0, total_frames_num, total_frames_num / n) ``` The final expression therefore evaluates `1 / 0`. ## Related PRs [#33746](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/33746) discussed frame-count alignment for preprocessed Qwen3-VL inputs with `do_sample_frames=False`. The discussion favored an informative validation error when the caller supplies an unaligned frame count. That PR was closed without being merged and does not handle the one-frame `video_url` sampling path in `Qwen2VLVideoBackend.compute_frames_index_to_sample()`. [#33956](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/33956) addressed a related zero-frame condition in Qwen3-VL's generic short-duration sampler. It was also closed without being merged and does not change this Qwen2-VL backend. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

 ### Summary

  With `mistralai/Voxtral-Mini-4B-Realtime-2602` on the Realtime API (`/v1/realtime`), the time
  per engine step grows
  linearly with the age of the session, with no plateau at the model's 8192-token sliding window.
  On our machine the
  median step goes from 26 ms to 59 ms over 12 minutes of audio, and p99 crosses the 80 ms
  real-time budget (one token
  per 80 ms of audio) at about 8 minutes, after which a single stream can no longer keep up. GPU
  utilisation *falls*
  while this happens.

  A py-spy profile of the EngineCore late in a session puts **~55 % of wall time in the
  scheduler**, in:

  ```
  schedule (vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py)
   └ NewRequestData.from_request (vllm/v1/core/sched/output.py)
      └ strip_covered_mm_data (vllm/multimodal/utils.py)      ← [maybe_strip(f) for f in
  mm_features]
         └ dataclasses.replace
  ```
 A realtime session appends one multimodal feature per 80 ms audio chunk (750 per minute) and is
  re-submitted to the
  worker on every step, so `strip_covered_mm_data` walks **all** accumulated features on
  **every** step and builds a
  fresh `dataclasses.replace` copy of each one already covered, without keeping the result. ~4 µs
  × 750 features ≈
  3 ms of pure Python per step per minute of session age, which matches the measured slope (2.99
  ms/min). Total work
  over a session is quadratic.

  `strip_covered_mm_data` came in with #52041. The decay reported in #39996 (0.19.x) suggests an
  older O(n) component
  existed as well; in 0.29.0 this function is the dominant one.

  ### Environment

  - vLLM 0.29.0 (PyPI wheel), torch 2.13.0+cu132, transformers 5.17.0, mistral-common 1.11.7,
  Python 3.12
  - RTX 3090, 4 vCPU of a Ryzen 7 2700 (Zen+). A slow core makes the effect large, but it is
  CPU-bound Python, so
    every host has it in proportion.

  ```
  VLLM_DISABLE_COMPILE_CACHE=1 vllm serve <model dir> --tokenizer-mode mistral --config-format
  mistral --load-format mistral \
    --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode": "PIECEWISE"}' --max-model-len 16384 --max-num-seqs 4
  \
    --max-num-batched-tokens 1024 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.60 --mm-processor-cache-gb 0
  --no-enable-prefix-caching
  ```
 ### Reproduction

  One realtime session, all audio sent at once, so the spacing of `transcription.delta` events is
  the per-step cost
  (a ~60-line script using only `websockets`; happy to share it). Nothing else attached to the
  server.

  | session age (min of audio) | 0–1 | 2–3 | 4–5 | 5–6 | 6–7 | 7–8 | 8–9 | 9–10 | 10–11 | 11–12 |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | step p50 (ms) | 26.4 | 31.7 | 37.2 | 40.0 | 43.2 | 46.0 | 48.9 | 52.1 | 55.1 | 58.9 |
  | step p95 (ms) | 28.4 | 34.0 | 41.9 | 45.8 | 52.8 | 69.5 | 76.9 | 83.9 | 90.9 | 100.7 |
  | step p99 (ms) | 29.9 | 39.8 | 55.0 | 61.7 | 69.8 | 78.1 | 82.1 | 88.5 | 95.7 | 107.6 |

  - Linear fit of p50 from minute 2: 23.8 ms + 2.99 ms/min.
  - No change of slope at 8192 tokens (≈ 10.9 min), while GPU KV cache usage plateaus at ~31 %,
  so it is neither
    attention nor KV growth.
  - GPU utilisation went 66 % → 48 % → 41 % (by thirds of the run) while the EngineCore process
  held ~75 % of one core.
  - `usage.completion_tokens` equals the number of deltas in every run (8970/8970), so no output
  merging is involved.

  ### Profile (py-spy `--nonblocking`, 200 Hz, 20 s each, EngineCore; the SAME session early and
  late)

  Same process, same request, same sampling; the only variable is how much audio the session has
  accumulated. Shares
  are inclusive (the three scheduler rows are one call chain).

  | share of EngineCore samples | early (~1 min of audio) | late (~9 min of audio) |
  |---|---|---|
  | `Scheduler.schedule()` | 16.9 % | **55.9 %** |
  | → `NewRequestData.from_request` | 16.9 % | 55.9 % |
  | → `strip_covered_mm_data` | 16.9 % | 55.9 % |
  | → → `dataclasses.replace` | 3.0 % | 11.4 % |
  | `execute_model` (the GPU forward) | 71.1 % | 37.8 % |
  | samples | 2391 | 2718 |

  The per-step time of that same session: p50 25 ms in its first minute, 50 ms in its ninth, 61
  ms in its thirteenth
  (p99 116 ms, beyond the 80 ms real-time budget). An independent earlier capture of a late
  session gave the same
  picture (`schedule()` 53 %, `execute_model` 41 %).

  At real-time pace (not burst), the same growth shows as +2.9 ms per minute of session age with
  one stream, +7.7 with
  two and +24 with four concurrent streams (7-minute sessions): concurrency multiplies how often
  the O(n) work runs.
 ### Suggested fix

  The set of covered features only ever grows, so the stripped form of a feature never changes
  once computed:

  - memoise it: keep the stripped copy next to the feature (or strip in place on the scheduler
  side for
    streaming-input requests, which never need the payload again), so a step touches only the
  *new* features; or
  - since features are ordered by `mm_position.offset`, remember the index of the first uncovered
  feature per request
    and only examine features from there on.

  Either makes the per-step cost O(new features) instead of O(all features).

### 🐛 Describe the bug ## 🐛 Describe the bug Multi-node TP=8 (2 nodes × 4 H200) serving DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash hangs indefinitely during engine startup, inside `ncclCommInitRank` graph/connection phase — before weight loading begins. The hang is deterministic and reproducible across 8+ restarts with different NCCL env configurations. Launch commands (per official multiprocessing multi-node docs) Head node: ```bash vllm serve /.cache/deepseek-v41-flash \ --served-model-name deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash \ --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 \ --tensor-parallel-size 8 --pipeline-parallel-size 1 \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 --enable-chunked-prefill \ --nnodes 2 --node-rank 0 \ --master-addr \ --trust-remote-code --disable-custom-all-reduce ``` Worker node: same + `--headless --node-rank 1`. Observed behavior (NCCL_DEBUG=TRACE) Both nodes bootstrap fine (TCP bootstrap OK, `commId` shared, 2 nodes detected). Then, with IB enabled: Even local_ranks (0, 2 / 4, 6) complete `Init COMPLETE`, log their `Trees`, and establish cross-node GDRDMA channels: `Channel 00/0 : 0[0] -> 4[0] [send] via NET/IB/4/GDRDMA`, `Channel 01/0 : 2[2] -> 6[2] [send] via NET/IB/5/GDRDMA` Odd local_ranks (1, 3 / 5, 7) stop after `comm 0x... rank N nRanks 8 nNodes 2 localRanks 4 localRank N MNNVL 0` + one `Trees` line — no Channel lines, no Init COMPLETE, indefinitely The APIServer loops forever on: `Waiting for 1 local, 0 remote core engine proc(s) to start.` Weight loading (`Loading safetensors`) never starts All worker threads sleep (futex / socket / ib_uverbs_event_read) — no spinning, no watchdog timeout, no error With `NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1` (Socket transport): the same hang, but now all 8 ranks block at the `MNNVL 0` boundary with zero Channel lines. The even/odd localRank asymmetry (the most distinctive part) On both nodes, exactly cudaDev 0 and cudaDev 2 (even local_ranks) complete init and own the cross-node GDRDMA channel pairs (0↔4 on one rail, 2↔6 on another). Odd local_ranks never establish their cross-node connections (1↔5, 3↔7). The pattern is stable across restarts and independent of: Variable tested Result `NCCL_IB_QPS_PER_CONNECTION=8` vs default ❌ no change `NCCL_CROSS_NIC=0` vs `1` ❌ no change `NCCL_NCHANNELS_PER_NET_PEER=4` vs `8` vs unset ❌ no change (worse: all ranks block) `NCCL_MAX/MIN_NCHANNELS=16/8` vs unset ❌ no change `NCCL_NET_GDR_LEVEL=SYS` + `NCCL_NET_GDR_READ=1` vs unset ❌ no change `NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1` (Socket transport) ❌ all 8 ranks block (earlier) `--disable-custom-all-reduce` ❌ no change Worker `--headless` (was missing initially — fixed) ❌ no change to the even/odd pattern env propagation ✅ verified — every NCCL_* var logged as "set by environment" on both nodes Ruled out TCP connectivity: bootstrap + `distributed_init_method=tcp://...:29501` reachable from both nodes (tested live) `/dev/shm`, UID, permissions: identical on both nodes GPU-NIC topology: NV6 intra-node, NICs PIX-adjacent to their NUMA-local GPUs, GDR works (GDRDMA channels DO form for even ranks) Env propagation: NCCL TRACE confirms every var read on both nodes Same model + same topology works on SGLang (NCCL 2.28.3) with identical k8s/network setup — 4 rails, GDRDMA, TP8/EP8 Hypothesis The rank-pair channel assignment during `ncclCommInitRank` graph-connect deadlocks when ranks need to establish cross-node QP connections in an order that requires the odd-rank pair's initiator to be a rank that is itself still initializing. ## Additional context Related: #53894 (DeepSeek-V4-Pro 2-node hang — `--disable-custom-all-reduce` fixed their case, not ours), #46097 (MiniMax multi-node collective deadlock — "ranks not in the same collective instance" hypothesis), #57423 (FlashInfer autotune rank-0-only cache — ours hangs earlier, at comm init) ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

items.title: [Bug]: An Anthropic messages test is not compatible with Anthropic SDK 1.x
items.body:
### Your current environment
The output of python collect_env.py vllm 0.28.0, 0.29.0 ```text Your output of `python collect_env.py` here ```
### 🐛 Describe the bug `tests/entrypoints/anthropic/test_messages.py::test_anthropic_streaming_cache_usage` passes `temperature=0.0` as a keyword argument to `AsyncMessages.create()`. That works on Anthropic Python SDK 0.x, but breaks on 1.x: ```text TypeError: AsyncMessages.create() got an unexpected keyword argument 'temperature' ``` This is a client-side SDK change, not a vLLM serving bug. Anthropic SDK 1.0 removed temperature / top_p / top_k from messages.create(), messages.stream(), and messages.parse(). Official migration notes: https://github.com/anthropics/anthropic-sdk-python/blob/main/MIGRATION.md#removed-deprecated-request-parameters Those sampling fields are gone from the method signature, not from the HTTP API. For older models that still honor them (including this test's served name claude-3-7-sonnet-latest), the documented replacement is extra_body: ```python # before client.messages.create(..., temperature=0.2) # after client.messages.create(..., extra_body={"temperature": 0.2}) ``` extra_body is merged into the JSON body by the SDK. vLLM already declares temperature on AnthropicMessagesRequest, so the server keeps parsing it as a normal field. No serving-side extra_body handling is required. vLLM depends on anthropic >= 0.71.0 (requirements/common.txt) with no <1 cap, so CI / downstream installs can resolve either 0.x or 1.x. extra_body exists on both generations, so this keeps the test working for both, but temperature= would get TypeError on 1.x. This test only asserts streaming prefix-cache usage (cache_read / cache_creation on message_delta). It does not inspect generated text, so it is indifferent to greedy vs default sampling. Dropping temperature entirely would also fix the TypeError This PR https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57780 keeps greedy via extra_body to stay closest to the original request. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

### 🐛 Describe the bug The watermarking feature was added in v0.30.0 (PR #54053, RFC #53916). This new feature allows per-request opt-out even when the server operator configured `--watermark-config`. A user can send `"watermarking": false` in a request, and the server disables the watermark for that request without any warning or log. This appears to be a gap in the initial implementation of the v0.30.0 watermarking feature. RFC #53916 states watermarking "is a modification of the sampling process, which cannot be modified by downstream consumers." The current implementation contradicts this — any API caller can modify the watermark behavior per-request. **Root cause:** `gpu_sampler.py` L41 reads `sampling_params.watermarking` directly. No code path checks the server's `--watermark-config` to override the per-request value. ```python # v1/watermarking/gpu_sampler.py:41 def add_request(self, req_idx, sampling_params): self.watermarking.np[req_idx] = sampling_params.watermarking # ← uses per-request value, no server-level enforcement ``` The `watermarking` field is exposed on all API endpoints: - `ChatCompletionRequest.watermarking` (protocol.py L270) - `CompletionRequest.watermarking` (protocol.py L78) - `ResponsesRequest.watermarking` (protocol.py L217) **Steps to reproduce:** ```bash # Start server with watermark enforced python -m vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server \ --model facebook/opt-125m \ --max-model-len 512 \ --watermark-config '{"key": 12345}' \ --port 8000 ``` ```python import requests MODEL = "facebook/opt-125m" URL = "http://localhost:8000" r1 = requests.post(URL + "/v1/completions", json={ "model": MODEL, "prompt": "Once upon a time", "max_tokens": 50, "temperature": 0.7, "seed": 42, "watermarking": True }) r2 = requests.post(URL + "/v1/completions", json={ "model": MODEL, "prompt": "Once upon a time", "max_tokens": 50, "temperature": 0.7, "seed": 42, "watermarking": False }) t1 = r1.json()["choices"][0]["text"] t2 = r2.json()["choices"][0]["text"] print(f"watermarking=True: {t1[:100]!r}") print(f"watermarking=False: {t2[:100]!r}") ``` ``` watermarking=True: ' for a great nation, it was the world’s greatest country, with a population of approximately 4 milli' watermarking=False: ', I fell in love with a girl.\nBut when I came to the realization that I had no idea what kind of a g' ``` The outputs differ because watermarking changes the sampling distribution (Gumbel-max). The server accepted `watermarking=False` (HTTP 200) without error, even though `--watermark-config` was set. **Expected behavior:** When `--watermark-config` is active, one of: 1. Ignore the per-request `watermarking` field and always watermark 2. Reject `watermarking=False` with HTTP 400 3. Add a `--watermark-enforce` flag that prevents per-request opt-out **Why this matters:** The v0.30.0 watermarking feature was built for regulatory compliance (EU AI Act Article 50(2), California SB 942 — see RFC #53916). Without server-level enforcement, operators who deploy `--watermark-config` for compliance cannot guarantee all outputs are watermarked. Any API user can silently bypass the policy. The server logs no warning when watermarking is disabled per-request. Since this feature just shipped in v0.30.0, fixing the enforcement gap now avoids breaking changes later. Related: RFC #53916, PR #54053, PR #56338 ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

items.title: [Bug]: vLLM does not ignore temperature, presence_penalty, and frequency_penalty for DeepSeek V4 series thinking mode, unlike the official DeepSeek API
items.body:
### Your current environment
The output of python collect_env.py ```text Your output of `python collect_env.py` here ```
### 🐛 Describe the bug Summary According to the official DeepSeek API documentation, the DeepSeek V4 series thinking mode does not support the temperature, presence_penalty, and frequency_penalty parameters. For backward compatibility, passing these parameters does not raise an error, but they have no effect. However, vLLM does not behave consistently with the DeepSeek API. When serving DeepSeek V4 series models in thinking mode, these parameters are still applied to sampling instead of being ignored. Expected behavior For DeepSeek V4 series thinking mode, vLLM should accept temperature, presence_penalty, and frequency_penalty without raising an error, but silently ignore them — matching the official DeepSeek API behavior. Actual behavior These parameters are still honored by the sampler, which can lead to different (and unexpected) outputs compared to the official API. Impact Users migrating from the official DeepSeek API to vLLM may get inconsistent results. Clients that rely on the documented "accepted but ignored" behavior may unintentionally change model output. Reproducibility across the official API and vLLM is broken for these models. Steps to reproduce Serve a DeepSeek V4 series model in thinking mode with vLLM. Send a request with different values of temperature (or presence_penalty / frequency_penalty). Observe that the output changes, whereas the official DeepSeek API would produce identical sampling behavior regardless of these values. Suggested fix Detect DeepSeek V4 series thinking mode and skip applying temperature, presence_penalty, and frequency_penalty in the sampling path, while still accepting them in the request schema for compatibility. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.
